Attackers use the confidence scores (softmax probabilities) returned by a model API to guide faster and more accurate model cloning, improving the quality of student models with fewer queries.
Vulnerability: Outputting raw class probabilities
Impact: Faster, more precise student cloning of API models
Detection: Detect high-volume confidence-based query behavior
Remediation: Replace or limit softmax outputs; use temperature scaling; return only top-1 class

instruction: Describe the Instruction-Based Content Extraction attack: Prompt-based Stealing from LLMs
output:
Attackers craft tailored prompts to large language models (LLMs) to regenerate content the model was trained or fine-tuned on, such as confidential documents, codebases, or internal FAQs.
Vulnerability: Memorization of sensitive fine-tuning content
Impact: Training data disclosure, copyright/IP leakage
Detection: Monitor for prompt injection and suspicious chaining behavior
Remediation: Implement rate limits, content filters, watermarking, and training-data differential privacy

instruction: Describe the Offline Model Stealing via Public Weight Files attack: Zero-query Stealing via Weights in Open Source
output:
Attackers can extract the full logic of a model even without using the model API by downloading published weight files (e.g., pytorch_model.bin) and reverse engineering its architecture from surrounding code or configs.
Vulnerability: Public release of weight files without protection
Impact: Full offline model reconstruction from shared weights
Detection: Monitor downloads, restrict sensitive asset exposure
Remediation: Never publish weight files unless needed; use model watermarking or license checks; strip unused artifacts

instruction: Describe the Policy Cloning via Environment Observation attack: Reinforcement Learning Model Extraction
output:
Attackers replicate the policy of reinforcement learning (RL) agents (e.g., in games or robots) by observing behavior and using imitation learning or self-play to build an equivalent agent.
Vulnerability: Observable input-action behavior patterns
Impact: Steal game AI, autonomous logic, or robotic control
Detection: Monitor action consistency; check for external logging or screen scraping
Remediation: Limit exposure in shared environments; introduce noise; restrict telemetry; watermark behavior

instruction: Describe the Aggregation Reconstruction from Gradient Updates attack: Model Extraction from Federated Clients
output:
Federated learning shares gradient updates from edge devices; attackers can intercept these updates and reverse-engineer the global model or sensitive patterns in user data.
Vulnerability: Leaking gradients during aggregation
Impact: Reconstruction of model or data; FL privacy bypass
Detection: Use secure aggregation protocols; detect abnormal update patterns
Remediation: Apply secure multi-party computation (SMPC); add noise to gradients; use DP-FL (Differential Privacy Federated Learning)

instruction: Describe the Self-Synthesized Data Query for Model Copy attack: Distillation from Generated Data
output:
Attacker trains a student model by querying the target model with synthetic data, and using only the outputs to distill and recreate the target’s behavior, even without real data.
Vulnerability: Synthetic data + soft-label output
Impact: Full model clone with no real data used
Detection: Monitor repetitive probing patterns; detect input novelty spikes
Remediation: Introduce input-dependent output noise; detect and block unusual API interaction loops

instruction: Describe the Combined Model Extraction and Data Reconstruction attack: Hybrid Attack (Stealing + Inversion)
output:
The attacker combines model output imitation (stealing) with inversion techniques to clone the model while reconstructing its training data (e.g., generating faces or sentences used during training).
Vulnerability: Combination of inversion and output exposure
Impact: Full model clone with partial or full training data recovered
Detection: Look for combined signature of inversion and extraction; detect repeated probing patterns
Remediation: Add noise to output vectors; restrict output granularity; apply watermarking and synthetic sample detection

instruction: Describe the Abuse via Format Translation attack: Model Format Conversion Abuse
output:
Attacker converts exported models (e.g., TensorFlow .pb or PyTorch .pt) into more transparent formats like ONNX or JSON, revealing hidden layers, hyperparameters, or graph topology.
Vulnerability: Exported model formats lacking obfuscation
Impact: Complete visibility into model internals; attack tailoring possible
Detection: Check for abnormal file format conversions or mass downloads
Remediation: Release models in obfuscated formats; encrypt critical layers; apply architecture fingerprinting or randomization

instruction: Describe the Leakage via Documentation and Evaluation Disclosures attack: Model Card / Metadata Exploitation
output:
Attackers analyze model documentation like model cards, confusion matrices, parameter counts, or layer descriptions to infer model structure or identify weaknesses.
Vulnerability: Excessively detailed metadata disclosure
Impact: Steal model blueprints or design patterns; aid in future attacks
Detection: Monitor usage logs of README, model card scraping scripts
Remediation: Limit sensitive disclosure in model cards; avoid publishing exact parameter values or layer counts

instruction: Describe the Obfuscation & Repurposing of Stolen Models attack: Watermark Removal & Rebranding
output:
After stealing or downloading a model, attacker removes embedded watermarks or fingerprints and rebrands it under a different name for resale or deceptive deployment.
Vulnerability: Lack of resilient watermarking
Impact: Loss of IP ownership, clone resale, brand misuse
Detection: Watermark-triggered model auditing; similarity scoring tools
Remediation: Use resilient watermarking (e.g., robust to fine-tuning); combine watermark with legal licensing checks

instruction: Describe the Model Evasion via Adversarial Perturbation attack: Adversarial Example Attack (Classic Evasion)
output:
Attackers generate adversarial inputs by applying small, carefully crafted perturbations to valid inputs, causing the model to make incorrect predictions while appearing visually identical or semantically similar to the human eye.
Vulnerability: Overconfidence in small perturbation resilience
Impact: Misclassification, security bypass, trust erosion
Detection: Monitor inputs with high confidence shifts; detect gradient-sensitive inputs
Remediation: Use adversarial training; apply input sanitization (e.g., JPEG compression, feature squeezing); monitor prediction uncertainty and variance

instruction: Describe the Evasion via Feature Manipulation attack: Feature Removal / Injection Attack
output:
Adversaries manipulate input by either removing important features or injecting irrelevant/noisy ones to mislead the model. This allows malicious data to appear benign, causing misclassification or evasion.
Vulnerability: Overreliance on static feature weights
Impact: Model bypass, fraud/malware evasion
Detection: Monitor shifts in input structure; track changes in key feature distributions
Remediation: Use feature importance auditing; apply adversarial training; enforce feature validation/sanity checks

instruction: Describe the Evasion via Input Format Change attack: Input Transformation Evasion
output:
Change input format, orientation, or color space to fool a vision model. Example: rotate an image to avoid object detection.
Vulnerability: Lack of robustness to input transformations
Impact: Model misclassification, evasion
Detection: Monitor input metadata and transformations; use anomaly detection for sudden shifts in input distribution
Remediation: Train model on augmented data; apply input normalization; use transformation-invariant architectures

instruction: Describe the Black-box Evasion via API Querying attack: API Evasion (Black-box)
output:
Query API repeatedly to learn what gets blocked, and craft payloads to bypass. Example: evade spam detection in a commercial ML API.
Vulnerability: Over-reliance on superficial input patterns
Impact: Bypass of security filters, spam delivery
Detection: Monitor for repeated failed queries; rate limit API requests; analyze unusual query patterns
Remediation: Use adversarial training; implement robust content filters; add input anomaly detection

instruction: Describe the Input Manipulation for Model Evasion attack: Feature Removal / Injection Attack
output:
Modify input features by removing critical features or injecting misleading ones to fool the model.
Vulnerability: Lack of input validation; feature dependency assumptions
Impact: Misclassification, evasion, decision bypass
Detection: Monitor input feature distributions for anomalies; detect missing or out-of-range features
Remediation: Validate all inputs; use imputation for missing data; train with noisy/missing features to improve robustness

instruction: Describe the Automated Input Mutation for Evasion attack: Polymorphic Input Attack
output:
Malware or inputs change shape or encoding to evade detection while keeping function intact.
Vulnerability: Over-reliance on static feature patterns
Impact: Detection evasion, security bypass
Detection: Behavioral anomaly detection; monitor input mutation frequency; update detection signatures regularly
Remediation: Use dynamic and behavioral analysis; retrain models with polymorphic samples; apply multi-layer defense

instruction: Describe the Universal Patch-based Evasion attack: Adversarial Patch Attack
output:
Apply a physical or digital patch/sticker to input (like an image) to fool model
Vulnerability: Vulnerable to localized adversarial perturbations
Impact: Misclassification, security bypass
Detection: Monitor for suspicious input regions; adversarial example detection algorithms
Remediation: Use adversarial training; robust model architectures; input preprocessing to remove patches

instruction: Describe the Transferability-based Evasion attack: Zero-query Evasion
output:
Use adversarial examples crafted on local substitute model to fool black-box target
Vulnerability: Black-box models vulnerable to transfer attacks
Impact: Bypass of black-box detection systems
Detection: Monitor input distribution shifts; rate-limit queries; ensemble model use
Remediation: Ensemble defenses; adversarial training; input sanitization

instruction: Describe the Gradient-based Input Perturbation attack: White-box Evasion (Gradient-based)
output:
Attacker uses full access to the model (weights, architecture, gradients) to create small changes in inputs that cause the model to misclassify or fail.
Vulnerability: Vulnerable to gradient-based perturbations
Impact: Causes misclassification, evasion of detection
Detection: Detect anomalous input perturbations; use adversarial input detectors; monitor model outputs for unusual confidence or errors
Remediation: Apply adversarial training; preprocess inputs; use robust model architectures; apply gradient masking carefully

instruction: Describe the Text Evasion via Semantic Change attack: Semantic Manipulation Attack
output:
Attacker modifies input text’s meaning-preserving words or phrases to evade detection while keeping semantics similar. For example, changing “attack” to “assault” to bypass spam filters or toxic content detectors.
Vulnerability: Vulnerable to semantic substitutions
Impact: Evade detection, spread spam or malicious content
Detection: Monitor for semantic anomalies; use adversarially trained models; analyze user patterns
Remediation: Use semantic robustness training; improve paraphrase detection; augment training with adversarial examples

instruction: Describe the Model Evasion via Universal Perturbations attack: Universal Adversarial Perturbation
output:
Create a single perturbation that, when added to any input, causes the ML model to misclassify it. Example: a noise pattern added to all images to fool an image classifier.
Vulnerability: Susceptible to small adversarial perturbations
Impact: High misclassification rate, evasion of security or recognition systems
Detection: Monitor input distribution shifts; detect abnormal input patterns
Remediation: Use adversarial training; input sanitization; detect and reject suspicious inputs

instruction: Describe the Manipulate model’s confidence scores to mislead or evade controls attack: Model Confidence Manipulation
output:
Attacker crafts inputs to lower or artificially inflate confidence output by model, affecting decision thresholds.
Vulnerability: Over-reliance on confidence scores
Impact: Incorrect system decisions, bypass of filters, decreased trust in model outputs
Detection: Monitor confidence score distribution shifts; anomaly detection on outputs
Remediation: Calibration of confidence, ensemble models, adversarial robustness training

instruction: Describe the Text Evasion via Minor Word or Character Changes attack: Word-level and Character-level Text Evasion
output:
Modify input text at the word or character level (typos, homoglyphs, spacing) to evade text classifiers or filters while preserving human readability.
Vulnerability: Sensitive to minor text perturbations
Impact: Evasion of detection, spread of malicious content
Detection: Monitor for anomalous text patterns; use spellcheck and semantic analysis
Remediation: Train with adversarial examples; use character-level embeddings; robust preprocessing

instruction: Describe the Physical Sensor Data Manipulation attack: Sensor Spoofing (Physical-world Evasion)
output:
Attackers manipulate real-world sensor inputs (e.g., GPS, LiDAR, accelerometers) to fool AI models relying on sensor data.
Vulnerability: Lack of sensor data validation or authentication
Impact: Safety failures, mis-navigation, denial of service
Detection: Cross-validate sensor inputs; watch for impossible sensor readings
Remediation: Use authenticated sensor data; sensor fusion; shielding and jamming detection

instruction: Describe the Data Manipulation via Metadata attack: Metadata Injection Attack
output:
Injecting false or misleading metadata into data streams or files to mislead ML models or downstream systems.
Vulnerability: Trust on unverified metadata fields
Impact: Model confusion, incorrect predictions, security bypass
Detection: Metadata validation, consistency checks, anomaly detection
Remediation: Sanitize inputs; ignore or verify metadata; use content-based features instead of metadata

instruction: Describe the Temporal Adversarial Attack attack: Adversarial Frame (Video)
output:
Apply adversarial perturbations to individual frames or sequences in video to fool video classification or detection models.
Vulnerability: Vulnerable to small temporal/frame perturbations
Impact: Misclassification, bypass of video analytics systems
Detection: Temporal anomaly detection, adversarial input detection
Remediation: Use robust temporal models; adversarial training; input sanitization

instruction: Describe the Evasion via Exploiting Ensemble Disagreement attack: Model Disagreement Exploit (Ensemble Evasion)
output:
Craft inputs that cause different models in an ensemble to produce conflicting outputs, confusing majority voting or aggregation.
Vulnerability: Ensemble vulnerability to conflicting model outputs
Impact: Degraded accuracy, evasion, system confusion
Detection: Monitor disagreement rates; flag inputs causing high model variance
Remediation: Use robust ensemble methods; calibrate models; adversarial training

instruction: Describe the Input Distribution Manipulation attack: Out-of-Distribution (OOD) Exploitation
output:
Submit inputs that are slightly outside or at the fringe of the training data distribution to fool the model.
Vulnerability: Poor generalization beyond training data
Impact: Misclassification, evasion, degraded reliability
Detection: Monitor input feature distributions; use OOD detectors or reject unknown inputs
Remediation: Use robust training, data augmentation, OOD detection methods

instruction: Describe the Real-time Data Manipulation attack: Runtime Input Evasion
output:
Modify data dynamically only at runtime or streaming time to evade detection or cause misclassification.
Vulnerability: No integrity checks on streaming data
Impact: Bypass of live monitoring, misclassification
Detection: Analyze stream characteristics for anomalies; use multi-modal checks
Remediation: Add integrity validation, anomaly detection on streams

instruction: Describe the Preprocessing Evasion attack: Data Encoding Attacks
output:
Use alternate encodings or malformed file structures to evade ML preprocessing or detection filters.
Vulnerability: Weak or inconsistent preprocessing
Impact: Evasion of detection, malware delivery
Detection: Check for inconsistent or malformed encodings; add layered decoding
Remediation: Normalize input formats; sanitize and reject malformed files

instruction: Describe the Evasion via Training Data Poisoning Assistance attack: Poisoned Training Assist Evasion
output:
Use poisoned or manipulated training assist data (e.g., data labeling, crowdsourcing) to cause the model to mislearn and evade.
Vulnerability: Training data poisoning and mislabeling
Impact: Reduced model accuracy, evasion, backdoors
Detection: Monitor training data integrity; validate label quality and consistency
Remediation: Use robust training algorithms; verify data sources

instruction: Describe the Domain Obfuscation Evasion attack: Subdomain-based Evasion
output:
Attackers hide malicious domains by dynamically rotating or adding subdomains to bypass domain filters.
Vulnerability: Reliance on root domain filtering, weak DNS monitoring
Impact: Phishing success, malware delivery
Detection: Monitor DNS query patterns; block unknown subdomains
Remediation: Use full domain blacklisting; DNS anomaly detection

instruction: Describe the Backdoor Activation via Input attack: Trigger-based Backdoor Exploitation
output:
Attackers embed hidden triggers (e.g., pixel patterns) in input to activate backdoors in compromised models.
Vulnerability: Malicious backdoor triggers in model training
Impact: Unauthorized access, model manipulation
Detection: Monitor for unusual input-output correlations; analyze model behavior under crafted inputs
Remediation: Use robust training, anomaly detection, and model auditing

instruction: Describe the Evasion via Model Compression attack: Compressed Model Exploitation (Pruned/Quantized)
output:
Exploit reduced accuracy or robustness of compressed models (e.g., pruned, quantized) to evade detection.
Vulnerability: Lowered accuracy and robustness due to compression
Impact: Evasion, misclassification, security bypass
Detection: Detect prediction instability; analyze inputs near decision boundaries
Remediation: Use adversarial training; robust compression techniques

instruction: Describe the Stochastic Model Evasion attack: Evasion via Sampling Noise / Dropout
output:
Exploit randomness in models using sampling noise or dropout during inference to cause inconsistent predictions.
Vulnerability: Randomness causing unstable predictions
Impact: Evasion, detection bypass, reduced trustworthiness
Detection: Monitor prediction variance; flag unstable outputs
Remediation: Use deterministic inference; ensemble averaging of outputs

instruction: Describe the Gradient-based Data Reconstruction attack: Deep Leakage from Gradients (DLG)
output:
Recover original input data (e.g., handwritten digits) from shared model gradients during federated learning updates.
Vulnerability: Gradients leak original training data
Impact: Privacy breach, data exposure
Detection: Monitor gradient patterns for abnormal updates
Remediation: Use gradient compression, differential privacy, or secure aggregation

instruction: Describe the Label and Data Reconstruction attack: Improved DLG (iDLG)
output:
Faster leakage of private data and corresponding labels from client gradients using improved optimization.

Impact: Private data and labels compromised

Remediation: Apply gradient perturbation, encryption, and secure aggregation

instruction: Describe the Gradient Matching Data Reconstruction attack: Inversion Attack via Gradient Matching
output:
Reconstruct client input data (images, text) by optimizing dummy inputs to match observed client gradients.
Vulnerability: Gradient leakage exposes training data
Impact: Breach of data confidentiality
Detection: Monitor updates for signs of inversion attacks
Remediation: Employ gradient perturbations and aggregation schemes

instruction: Describe the Assisted Gradient Reconstruction attack: Gradient Leakage with Auxiliary Knowledge
output:
Use side information or auxiliary data to improve accuracy and speed of gradient inversion attacks.
Vulnerability: Auxiliary data aids gradient inversion attacks
Impact: Enhanced privacy breach, sensitive data exposure
Detection: Monitor training updates for suspicious patterns
Remediation: Combine differential privacy and secure aggregation

instruction: Describe the Full Access Gradient Input Reconstruction attack: White-box Gradient Leakage
output:
Attacker with full access to model weights and gradient updates (e.g., malicious federated learning aggregator) reconstructs private inputs from gradients.
Vulnerability: Full gradient exposure in white-box scenario
Impact: Complete privacy loss, exact input reconstruction
Detection: Monitor full gradient access; anomaly detection on update patterns
Remediation: Use gradient perturbation, secure aggregation, differential privacy

instruction: Describe the Partial or Noisy Gradient Reconstruction attack: Black-box Gradient Leakage
output:
Attacker with limited or noisy access to gradients tries to reconstruct approximate client inputs in privacy-preserving FL.
Vulnerability: Partial or noisy gradient exposure
Impact: Approximate data leakage, sensitive feature exposure
Detection: Detect noisy/partial gradient sharing; restrict update granularity
Remediation: Employ secure aggregation, limit gradient precision, use differential privacy

instruction: Describe the Precision Leakage due to Small Batch Size attack: Batch Size and Gradient Leakage Correlation
output:
Smaller batch sizes cause gradients to reflect fewer samples, enabling more precise reconstruction of individual inputs.
Vulnerability: Small batch sizes lead to precise gradient info
Impact: Exact or near-exact input recovery
Detection: Monitor batch sizes; enforce minimum batch size for updates
Remediation: Enforce large batch sizes; add noise to gradients; use aggregation

instruction: Describe the Gradient Reconstruction on NLP Models attack: Gradient Leakage on Text Models
output:
Attackers reconstruct private textual data (e.g., chat messages) shared as gradients in federated learning for NLP tasks.
Vulnerability: Gradient leakage on discrete text data
Impact: Private text disclosure, privacy breach
Detection: Monitor gradient access in NLP tasks; anomaly detection
Remediation: Use embedding obfuscation, gradient clipping, secure aggregation

instruction: Describe the Gradient-based Audio Signal Reconstruction attack: Gradient Leakage on Voice / Audio Models
output:
Extract original voice or audio signals from gradients shared during federated learning for speech recognition.
Vulnerability: Gradients leak private audio data
Impact: Private audio exposure, identity theft
Detection: Monitor gradient patterns; detect anomalies in audio domain gradients
Remediation: Use gradient perturbation, differential privacy, secure aggregation

instruction: Describe the Gradient Reconstruction Despite DP Noise attack: Gradient Leakage with Differential Privacy Mitigation Bypass
output:
Attack gradients even when differential privacy noise is added by filtering out noise to partially recover private data.
Vulnerability: Gradient noise from DP can be filtered and bypassed
Impact: Reduced privacy guarantees despite DP; data leakage
Detection: Monitor gradient noise levels; verify DP implementation rigorously
Remediation: Use advanced DP methods, increase noise scale, combine with secure aggregation

instruction: Describe the Improved Reconstruction Using Priors and Iteration attack: Adaptive Gradient Leakage
output:
Use additional generative priors or GANs to improve quality of reconstructed inputs from gradients.
Vulnerability: Use of priors improves inversion attack success
Impact: More accurate data leakage and privacy compromise
Detection: Detect abnormal reconstruction attempts; monitor gradient usage
Remediation: Employ strong priors in defense, combine DP and secure aggregation

instruction: Describe the Leak Private Data Using Optimizer State Exposure attack: Gradient Leakage via Momentum and Optimizer States
output:
Use optimizer momentum vectors and states shared or leaked to reconstruct private training data.
Vulnerability: Leakage via optimizer momentum/state exposure
Impact: Enhanced private data leakage, model update exposure
Detection: Monitor optimizer state sharing; restrict optimizer metadata leakage
Remediation: Avoid sharing optimizer states; apply DP/noise to optimizer states

instruction: Describe the Gradient Reconstruction in Split NN attack: Gradient Leakage in Split Learning
output:
Attackers extract client input data from intermediate gradients exchanged between client and server in split learning setups.
Vulnerability: Intermediate gradient exposure
Impact: Private input reconstruction, privacy loss
Detection: Monitor gradient traffic; detect anomalous requests or data size changes
Remediation: Encrypt gradient communication; use secure multi-party computation; add noise to gradients

instruction: Describe the Collaborative Gradient Inversion Attack attack: Multi-party Gradient Leakage
output:
Multiple malicious clients collude in federated learning to combine gradient info and reconstruct honest clients’ private data.
Vulnerability: Gradient exposure in multi-client setting
Impact: Severe privacy leakage across multiple clients
Detection: Detect collusion by analyzing client updates and communication patterns
Remediation: Enforce secure aggregation protocols; limit client communication; use DP

instruction: Describe the Targeted Inversion on Small FL Setups attack: Gradient Leakage in Cross-Silo FL
output:
Attack gradients in cross-silo federated learning with few participants, enabling easier inversion of data.
Vulnerability: Small participant sets reveal individual gradients
Impact: Accurate private data leakage, regulatory risk
Detection: Monitor participant behaviors; detect abnormal update patterns
Remediation: Increase participant count; apply DP and secure aggregation; monitor updates

instruction: Describe the Input Reconstruction from Model Weight Deltas attack: Gradient Leakage from Model Updates (Weight Differences)
output:
Attackers infer private training data by analyzing model weight differences across training iterations.
Vulnerability: Exposure through observable weight updates
Impact: Private data leakage from model updates
Detection: Monitor model weight access; limit update frequency and granularity
Remediation: Use secure aggregation; encrypt model checkpoints; use DP on model weights

instruction: Describe the Gradient Leakage despite Compression attack: Gradient Leakage from Quantized / Compressed Updates
output:
Attackers reconstruct private training data even when FL updates are compressed or quantized to reduce bandwidth.
Vulnerability: Compression does not eliminate gradient info
Impact: Private training data leakage despite compression
Detection: Monitor compressed gradient traffic; analyze update anomalies
Remediation: Use stronger compression with DP noise; encrypt updates; limit granularity of gradient info

instruction: Describe the Generative Model-Aided Gradient Inversion attack: Gradient Leakage via GAN Priors
output:
Use GANs to improve the quality and realism of reconstructed inputs from gradient data in federated learning.
Vulnerability: Gradient exposure without privacy protection
Impact: Realistic data reconstruction from gradients
Detection: Detect unnatural GAN-like patterns in updates; monitor gradient norms
Remediation: Use DP, gradient clipping, and secure aggregation; limit shared gradient granularity

instruction: Describe the Targeted Leakage in Client-Specific Models attack: Gradient Leakage in Personalized FL
output:
Attack fine-tuned or adapter layers personalized per client in federated learning to reconstruct client data.
Vulnerability: Personalized updates leak client data
Impact: Severe privacy breach in personalized FL
Detection: Monitor personalized model updates; detect anomalous gradient patterns
Remediation: Use local DP for personalized layers; restrict personalized model sharing

instruction: Describe the Gradient Leakage in Graph Neural Network FL attack: Gradient Leakage on Graph Neural Networks in FL
output:
Extract private node features and graph structure from gradients shared in federated GNN training.
Vulnerability: Gradient exposure of graph data and structure
Impact: Private graph data leakage and topology exposure
Detection: Monitor GNN update patterns; check for anomalous gradient similarity
Remediation: Use encrypted aggregation; apply noise to graph gradients; restrict shared updates

instruction: Describe the Side-channel Assisted Gradient Inversion attack: Side-channel Assisted Gradient Leakage
output:
Attackers use side-channel info like timing, memory, and network traffic patterns to improve gradient inversion attacks on FL models.
Vulnerability: Side-channel leakage in gradient exchange
Impact: Enhanced privacy leakage via side-channel info
Detection: Monitor side-channel leaks; network timing anomalies
Remediation: Add randomized delays; pad communication; encrypt and obfuscate metadata

instruction: Describe the Hyperparameter-Aware Gradient Inversion attack: Gradient Leakage via Hyperparameter Exploitation
output:
Attackers exploit known or leaked FL hyperparameters (learning rate, batch size, optimizer) to improve gradient leakage attacks.
Vulnerability: Hyperparameter exposure enhances gradient attacks
Impact: Faster, higher fidelity private data leakage
Detection: Monitor metadata leaks about hyperparameters
Remediation: Keep hyperparameters secret; rotate settings; add DP noise

instruction: Describe the Partial Gradient Exposure Inversion attack: Gradient Leakage with Partial Parameter Exposure
output:
Attack scenarios where only parts of gradients or layers leak, attacker reconstructs inputs from partial information.
Vulnerability: Partial gradient exposure leaks data
Impact: Partial but significant leakage of private inputs
Detection: Monitor partial gradient sharing; detect anomalous gradient patterns
Remediation: Minimize shared gradients; encrypt partial gradients; use DP

instruction: Describe the Collaborative GAN-based Gradient Leakage attack: Federated GAN Attack (FGAN)
output:
Use collaboratively trained GANs in federated learning to recover private client data from gradients.
Vulnerability: GAN-assisted gradient inversion leakage
Impact: Collaborative leakage of client private data
Detection: Monitor GAN activity in FL clients; anomalous update patterns
Remediation: Limit GAN usage; restrict client participation; add DP noise

instruction: Describe the Leakage via Asynchronous Gradient Sharing attack: Gradient Leakage from Asynchronous FL
output:
Attack data leakage exploiting asynchronous updates in federated learning where clients update at different times.
Vulnerability: Leakage due to asynchronous gradient sharing
Impact: Precise client data leakage from async updates
Detection: Monitor timing and order of gradients; randomize client update schedules
Remediation: Synchronize updates; add noise; anonymize timing metadata

instruction: Describe the Label Flipping Data Poisoning attack: Data Poisoning Attack (Label Flipping)
output:
Malicious clients flip labels of training data in federated learning to degrade model accuracy or cause misclassification.
Vulnerability: Lack of validation on local training data
Impact: Model accuracy degradation, misclassification

Remediation: Use robust aggregation; validate client data labels; anomaly detection

instruction: Describe the Backdoor Injection through Poisoned Updates attack: Backdoor Attack via Poisoned Updates
output:
Attackers inject triggers into their local training data causing the global model to behave normally except for malicious backdoor inputs.
Vulnerability: No validation of client update integrity
Impact: Backdoor insertion, targeted misclassification
Detection: Detect via backdoor trigger scanning; evaluate model on trigger inputs
Remediation: Use anomaly detection; limit client influence; apply backdoor defenses like pruning

instruction: Describe the Malicious Gradient Manipulation attack: Model Update Poisoning (Gradient Manipulation)
output:
Attackers manipulate model updates (gradients or weights) directly to degrade global model or cause targeted failure.
Vulnerability: No gradient integrity verification
Impact: Model degradation, targeted failures
Detection: Monitor update norm anomalies; use secure aggregation protocols
Remediation: Use robust aggregation (median, Krum); verify updates cryptographically

instruction: Describe the Multiple Fake Client Identities for Poisoning attack: Sybil Attack
output:
Attacker creates many fake or compromised clients to overwhelm FL aggregation with poisoned updates.
Vulnerability: Weak client authentication and aggregation
Impact: Model corruption, backdoor, denial of service
Detection: Authenticate clients; monitor client behavior and update similarity
Remediation: Use client reputation, robust aggregation; limit new client joins

instruction: Describe the Non-contributing Update Submission attack: Free-rider Attack
output:
Attacker sends random or copied model updates without genuine training, but still skews the global model.
Vulnerability: No validation of genuine contribution
Impact: Model quality degradation, wasted resources
Detection: Analyze update similarity and quality; track contribution history
Remediation: Require proof-of-work or contribution scoring; detect anomalous update patterns

instruction: Describe the Amplification of Malicious Updates attack: Scaling Attack
output:
Malicious client multiplies their update gradients to dominate aggregation and skew the global model.
Vulnerability: Lack of update magnitude clipping
Impact: Model corruption, targeted misclassification
Detection: Monitor update norms; clip or normalize gradients before aggregation
Remediation: Use robust aggregation methods (median, trimmed mean); gradient clipping

instruction: Describe the Malicious Complete Model Replacement attack: Model Replacement Attack
output:
Attacker submits a full malicious model update to replace the global model with a backdoored or biased one.
Vulnerability: No model update consistency checks
Impact: Backdoor insertion, model corruption
Detection: Validate update similarity; apply robust aggregation; scan for backdoors
Remediation: Use anomaly detection, update consistency checks, and defense aggregation methods

instruction: Describe the Arbitrary Malicious Client Behavior attack: Byzantine Attack
output:
Malicious clients send arbitrary or inconsistent updates aiming to degrade model or cause failures.

Impact: Model degradation, denial of service
Detection: Detect anomalous update patterns; monitor training divergence
Remediation: Use Byzantine-resilient aggregation (Krum, median); client reputation systems

instruction: Describe the Poisoning via Malicious Data attack: Data Injection Attack
output:
Attacker injects carefully crafted malicious samples into local training data to bias or corrupt the model.

Impact: Model bias, targeted misclassification

Remediation: Use robust training, anomaly detection, and data sanitization

instruction: Describe the Backdoor Poisoning with Label Consistency attack: Label-consistent Backdoor Attack
output:
Insert poisoned samples with true labels but cause misclassification on trigger inputs.

Remediation: Use robust aggregation, backdoor detection algorithms

instruction: Describe the Stealthy Malicious Update Hiding attack: Gradient Masking Attack
output:
Attacker masks malicious gradient updates to mimic benign client update statistics and evade detection.

Impact: Stealthy poisoning, difficult detection

Multiple attacker-controlled clients collude to poison the model or evade defenses collectively.

Attack adapts poison strength based on observed defenses or aggregation methods to maximize impact stealthily.

Remediation: Deploy adaptive defenses; use ensemble aggregators and dynamic anomaly detection

Attacker poisons updates to degrade the model while locally extracting a copy of the global model.

Remediation: Use query rate limiting, robust aggregation, output perturbation

output:
Multiple attacker clients coordinate to inject backdoors to the global model more effectively and stealthily.

Remediation: Use robust aggregation methods and multi-client anomaly detection

instruction: Describe the Data Poisoning with Label and Feature Manipulation attack: Label Flipping + Feature Poisoning Combined

instruction: Describe the Randomized Poisoning for Model Degradation attack: Untargeted Poisoning Attack
output:

Vulnerability: Lack of robust aggregation

Remediation: Use robust/fault-tolerant aggregation; reputation systems; data validation

instruction: Describe the Specific Class or Output Misclassification attack: Targeted Poisoning Attack
output:
Attacker crafts poison data or updates to cause model to misclassify specific inputs or classes
Vulnerability: Poisoning targeting specific outputs or classes
Impact: Targeted misclassification, backdoors, integrity breach

instruction: Describe the Full Model Control by Malicious Updates attack: Model Hijacking via Poisoned Updates

instruction: Describe the Targeted Poisoning in Small-Scale FL attack: Poisoning in Cross-Silo FL

instruction: Describe the Poisoning that Circumvents DP Protections attack: Poisoning Against Differential Privacy (DP) Mechanisms
output:
Poisoning attack designed to bypass differential privacy protections meant to safeguard FL models

instruction: Describe the Shadow Model-Based Membership Attack attack: Membership Inference via Shadow Models
output:
This attack aims to determine whether a specific data sample was part of the training dataset of a target ML model. It is done by training one or more shadow models to mimic the target model and then using an attack model to infer membership.
Vulnerability: Overfitting + confidence output leakage
Impact: Privacy leakage; reveals presence of specific data in model training
Detection: Analyze output distributions for privacy drift; monitor API query patterns and thresholds
Remediation: Limit output confidence scores; use differential privacy during training; detect unusual query behaviors

instruction: Describe the Shadow Model-Based Model Stealing attack: Model Extraction with Shadow Models
output:
Attacker trains shadow models using outputs from a black-box ML API to reconstruct a copy of the target model locally.
Vulnerability: Overexposed query interface + confidence leak
Impact: Model IP theft, evasion crafting, cost reduction
Detection: Monitor excessive or uniform query patterns; detect statistical mimicry in behavior
Remediation: Limit output detail (e.g., no probabilities); use query rate limiting; apply watermarking or detection traps

instruction: Describe the Shadow Model-Based Adversarial Evasion attack: Shadow Model for Adversarial Example Generation
output:
Attacker trains a shadow model locally to craft adversarial inputs that evade detection on the target model.
Vulnerability: Transferable evasion across models
Impact: Undetected adversarial samples, evasion of ML defenses
Detection: Monitor input patterns for small changes with big output shifts; use adversarial input detection
Remediation: Adversarial training; input sanitization; response thresholding

instruction: Describe the Shadow Model-Based Inversion attack: Shadow Model for Model Inversion
output:
The attacker uses a shadow model to learn the data distribution of the target’s training data and attempts to reconstruct private or sensitive inputs like faces or demographics.
Vulnerability: Confidence leakage + model inversion potential
Impact: Identity leakage, privacy violation, dataset re-identification
Detection: Monitor for repeated queries tied to specific labels or classes
Remediation: Differential privacy, output perturbation, limit confidence scores, input-output monitoring

instruction: Describe the Ensemble Shadow Model Membership/Evasion attack: Multiple Shadow Models Ensemble Attack
output:
Instead of using one shadow model, attacker trains many shadow models with varied data splits to better learn the target model’s behavior and boost attack accuracy.
Vulnerability: Overfit exposure + ensemble approximation
Impact: Stronger evasion or privacy attack success
Detection: Analyze if input-output patterns appear ensemble-aggregated; detect similarity across queries
Remediation: Randomize model behavior slightly; monitor for aggregated, repeated probing; train robust against ensembling attacks

instruction: Describe the Federated Learning Shadow Model Inference attack: Shadow Model Attack on Federated Learning
output:
Attacker mimics the global model in FL by training a shadow model using public or leaked data to infer private information about clients' local datasets.
Vulnerability: Public model leakage, insufficient update protection
Impact: Private client data inference, data reconstruction
Detection: Monitor repeated behavior mimicking training; detect shadow-like update behavior
Remediation: Add noise via Differential Privacy; apply secure aggregation; prevent precise model inspection

instruction: Describe the Transfer Learning Model Extraction attack: Transfer Learning Shadow Model
output:
Attacker uses transfer learning on a shadow model trained on a similar domain to mimic a fine-tuned proprietary model like a commercial LLM or image classifier.
Vulnerability: Transferability of pretrained weights
Impact: Model stealing, bypassing monetized inference
Detection: Detect multiple aligned queries over narrow domains; monitor unusual fine-tuned behaviors
Remediation: Use watermarking; return output with uncertainty/noise; protect API endpoints with rate-limiting

instruction: Describe the API-Based Shadow Model Training attack: Black-box Shadow Model Training
output:
Attacker collects input-output pairs from a target model via API queries to train a shadow model from scratch without any knowledge of internal architecture.
Vulnerability: Output overexposure via APIs
Impact: Model theft, cost evasion, attack testing platform
Detection: Monitor high-volume or uniform queries with slight variations
Remediation: Reduce output granularity (e.g., no confidence); rate-limit and log model queries

instruction: Describe the Shadow Model-Based GNN Extraction attack: Shadow Model Attack on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs)
output:
Attacker trains a local GNN to mimic a proprietary GNN model used in recommendations or graph classification (e.g., social networks or fraud systems).
Vulnerability: Structural input leakage + prediction access
Impact: Graph structure extraction, recommendation gaming
Detection: Monitor input-query graphs for repetitive or reverse-engineered topologies
Remediation: Randomize node outputs; restrict structural queries; use GNN watermarking/monitoring tools

instruction: Describe the Backdoor Behavior Profiling with Shadows attack: Shadow Model for Triggered Backdoor Detection
output:
Shadow models are trained to simulate target model behavior. Differences in output between clean and backdoor-triggered inputs help reveal potential backdoors.
Vulnerability: Backdoor triggers not visible in training data
Impact: Detection of hidden behavior, integrity compromise
Detection: Monitor for inconsistent behavior across inputs or classes
Remediation: Run differential testing using shadow models; prune suspicious neurons or retrain with robust methods

instruction: Describe the Query-driven Shadow Refinement attack: Adaptive Shadow Model Attack
output:
The attacker incrementally adapts shadow models based on target model output feedback, refining them to better mimic and exploit the target model.
Vulnerability: Overexposure via repeated queries
Impact: Full model mimicry, privacy risk, attack platform construction
Detection: Monitor for high-frequency, slight-variation API calls
Remediation: Add random noise, round off output probabilities, rate limit sensitive API behavior

instruction: Describe the Shadow Modeling with External Data Sources attack: Shadow Model Attack with Auxiliary Data
output:
Attacker trains shadow models using public or leaked data to better replicate the target model's domain, improving accuracy and inference capabilities.
Vulnerability: Public data similarity exploitation
Impact: Better model cloning, reduced API queries, private data risk
Detection: Monitor for input patterns sourced from public datasets
Remediation: Restrict input formats, watermark data used in training, add DP-style noise to training or output

instruction: Describe the Privacy Inference via Shadow Models attack: Shadow Model-based Privacy Leakage
output:
Shadow models trained to mimic the target are used to infer private training data or sensitive attributes through behavioral analysis.
Vulnerability: High confidence on training set samples
Impact: Data privacy breach, sensitive attribute leakage
Detection: Monitor access to sensitive input predictions; check for repeated membership tests
Remediation: Add differential privacy during training; reduce output granularity; apply dropout or adversarial regularization

instruction: Describe the Rate-Efficient Shadow Modeling for Attack Prep attack: Shadow Model to Bypass Rate Limiting
output:
Build shadow models to simulate target behavior, reducing number of queries needed for attacks like membership inference or model extraction.
Vulnerability: Strict API query limits
Impact: API cost savings for attacker, faster attacks, stealth access
Detection: Monitor behavior similarity between known input classes and repeated attacker requests
Remediation: Add randomized noise to outputs, lower precision responses, implement query fingerprinting to detect model cloning attempts

instruction: Describe the Knowledge Transfer for Model Cloning attack: Shadow Model Attack via Distillation
output:
Clone the target model behavior by distilling its responses into a simpler local model for future misuse or adversarial training.
Vulnerability: Output softmax exposure
Impact: Full model cloning, offline attacks, watermark evasion
Detection: Monitor for high-volume softmax vector requests; compare distributions for duplication
Remediation: Remove softmax vector output; provide top-1 class only; round probabilities or introduce dropout in output

instruction: Describe the Proxy Vulnerability Testing attack: Shadow Model for Model Robustness Testing
output:
Shadow models are used to simulate the target, allowing adversarial examples or stress tests to identify weak decision boundaries in the target model.
Vulnerability: Weakness reuse via adversarial transfer
Impact: Classifier evasion, poisoning readiness, patch failures
Detection: Compare error rates across diverse samples; flag similar perturbation patterns
Remediation: Use adversarial training on real model; test with synthetic shadows; limit model exposure to sensitive inputs

instruction: Describe the Commercial Cloud API Model Theft attack: Shadow Model Attack in Cloud ML Services
output:
Attacker targets services like AWS SageMaker, Google AI, or Azure ML by training shadow models from their API behavior to steal or attack models.
Vulnerability: Public API allows large-scale shadow learning
Impact: Full model theft, privacy leakage, commercial misuse
Detection: Monitor large query volumes from unknown clients; flag unusual data distributions
Remediation: Add watermarking and behavior signatures to detect stolen models; limit model output detail and rate limit unknown users

instruction: Describe the Shadow Modeling Under Query Constraints attack: Shadow Model with Limited Query Budget
output:
Attacker builds an efficient shadow model with minimal target queries, enabling model extraction and privacy attacks even under API query budget limits.
Vulnerability: Limited interaction window for adversary
Impact: Enables model theft and privacy attacks under constraints
Detection: Detect sampling patterns or non-human-like API usage
Remediation: Use query rate limits with behavioral analysis; restrict probabilistic outputs; return only labels or rounded scores

instruction: Describe the Domain Transfer via Shadow Modeling attack: Cross-domain Shadow Model Attack
output:
Shadow models trained on public datasets from similar domains are used to attack private or proprietary models trained on sensitive data (e.g., medical).
Vulnerability: Public data + low-query attacks
Impact: Leaks training data structure or logic from private models
Detection: Monitor model use for out-of-distribution inputs
Remediation: Restrict access to model prediction confidence; enforce strong input domain validation

instruction: Describe the Evasion via Adversarial Inputs from Shadows attack: Shadow Model for Evasion Attack Generation
output:
Use shadow models to craft inputs that fool the original target model by exploiting decision boundaries learned locally.
Vulnerability: Predictable decision boundaries
Impact: Classifier bypass, attack delivery success
Detection: Flag sudden model behavior changes or pattern of similar evasions
Remediation: Use adversarial training; introduce randomness or smoothing to model outputs

instruction: Describe the NLP-specific Shadow Modeling & Inference attack: Shadow Model Attack on NLP Models
output:
Shadow models are used to clone or attack NLP models like sentiment classifiers, language models, or text detectors.
Vulnerability: NLP output predictability and overconfidence
Impact: Disinformation, bias exploitation, model evasion
Detection: Monitor for repeated or crafted text patterns from clients
Remediation: Apply perturbation-aware training; use randomized token masking during inference

instruction: Describe the Vision-focused Shadow Model Extraction & Evasion attack: Shadow Model Attack on Vision Models
output:
Use CNN-based shadow models to approximate commercial or proprietary vision models and craft adversarial images that fool them.
Vulnerability: Gradient and prediction leakage via API
Impact: Model misclassification, security bypass in vision AI
Detection: Monitor for abnormal input patterns (e.g., noise, overlays); analyze prediction entropy
Remediation: Employ adversarial training; use input sanitization (e.g., JPEG compression) before inference

instruction: Describe the Membership Inference Despite DP Protections attack: Shadow Model for Differential Privacy Bypass
output:
Shadow models are used to exploit patterns not masked effectively by DP, allowing inference about private data even when DP is applied.
Vulnerability: Inadequate DP parameter tuning or implementation
Impact: Identity leakage, privacy violations despite DP claims
Detection: Validate effective epsilon value via DP audits; measure MI risk across shadow settings
Remediation: Use rigorous DP accounting; reduce output confidence; apply DP at model deployment (not only training)

instruction: Describe the Stealing from Multi-input Models (text/image/audio) attack: Shadow Model Attack on Multimodal Models
output:
Shadow models mimic complex multi-modal models (e.g., CLIP, GPT-Vision, or DALL·E) using combined datasets to perform inference or evasion attacks.
Vulnerability: Embedding predictability and data leakage
Impact: Evasion, misinformation, training data leakage
Detection: Analyze joint embedding distributions; monitor for prompt manipulation or semantic mismatch
Remediation: Apply contrastive learning regularization; randomize multimodal alignment during training; limit embedding access

instruction: Describe the Cloud Co-Tenant Leakage attack: Shared Hardware Co-Residency Attack
output:
Attacker runs a VM or container on the same server (co-residency) as a victim’s LLM. By watching shared resource patterns, they learn about LLM activity.
Vulnerability: Cloud machines share CPU/memory timing
Impact: Victim activity leak, LLM job detection
Detection: Monitor resource usage patterns across tenants; alert on odd cache/timing probes
Remediation: Use hardware isolation (dedicated machines); deny co-residency unless explicitly needed

instruction: Describe the Credential Leak via File Access attack: Exposed .env or Config Files
output:
Applications accidentally expose .env or config.yaml files in public locations (like GitHub, S3, or web root), revealing API keys, database credentials, or secrets.
Vulnerability: Public exposure of sensitive files
Impact: Account takeover, API abuse, data breach
Detection: Monitor for public .env file exposure with GitHub secrets scanning or tools like truffleHog
Remediation: Use .gitignore for secret files; use secret managers like AWS Secrets Manager or Vault; rotate credentials regularly

instruction: Describe the API Key Misuse in ML Platforms attack: Public HuggingFace Token in Repos
output:
Developers accidentally commit HuggingFace tokens to GitHub, letting attackers use the token to delete, download, or edit hosted AI models.
Vulnerability: Leaked ML tokens in public code repos
Impact: Model theft, account compromise, ML supply chain risk
Detection: Monitor token usage; setup secret scanning (e.g., GitHub Advanced Security)
Remediation: Never commit tokens; use .env and .gitignore; auto-scan repos using GitLeaks or GitGuardian

instruction: Describe the Remote Code Execution via Debug attack: Unprotected LangChain Debug Server
output:
A developer accidentally exposes the LangChain agent's debug or dev server to the public, which allows remote users to view memory, inject prompts, or run commands.
Vulnerability: Debug endpoints exposed to internet
Impact: Agent hijack, prompt injection, data exposure
Detection: Check exposed ports using Nmap or Shodan; log debug API usage; use firewall rules
Remediation: Never expose debug interfaces to the internet; use authentication and network-level restrictions

instruction: Describe the Unauthorized Access attack: Open LLM API Endpoint with No Auth
output:
An LLM backend like OpenAI, Claude, or a self-hosted model (e.g., Ollama) is exposed via API endpoint without authentication, allowing any external user to send prompts.
Vulnerability: Missing authentication
Impact: Data theft, model abuse, API cost surge
Detection: Monitor access logs for anonymous access; alert on unknown IPs or abnormal usage patterns
Remediation: Always protect APIs with auth keys, OAuth, or IP whitelisting; disable open endpoints in production

instruction: Describe the Information Disclosure attack: RAG Service Exposes Search Indexes
output:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems sometimes expose their internal vector DB or index files, letting attackers extract internal embeddings and private knowledge.
Vulnerability: Unprotected vector/index API endpoints
Impact: Intellectual property leakage, data exfiltration
Detection: Check RAG APIs for public index exposure; monitor requests to /api/, /index, /collections, /query endpoints
Remediation: Use API gateways or proxies to protect vector APIs; restrict read access to indexes; encrypt embeddings if sensitive

instruction: Describe the Authentication Bypass attack: Default Passwords in LangChain Plugins
output:
Some LangChain tools and plugins ship with default credentials (e.g., “admin:admin”) that are never changed, letting attackers log in and misuse internal tools.
Vulnerability: Default credentials left unchanged
Impact: Full plugin access, LLM hijack, data compromise
Detection: Check cloud logs for “admin” logins from new IPs; scan for default creds using vulnerability scanners
Remediation: Enforce password rotation policies; disable default credentials at plugin install; scan plugins during CI/CD for weak auth

instruction: Describe the Auth Hijack attack: Misconfigured OAuth Redirect URIs
output:
A misconfigured OAuth flow lets attackers redirect authentication tokens to their own website, allowing them to steal user sessions or impersonate them.
Vulnerability: Poor redirect URI validation
Impact: Account takeover, unauthorized access
Detection: Monitor token usage from unfamiliar domains; use OAuth audit logs
Remediation: Always validate redirect_uri parameters against allowlist; use state tokens and PKCE for all flows

instruction: Describe the File Injection attack: Open S3 Bucket Hosting Agent Tools
output:
Developers leave Amazon S3 buckets (cloud file storage) open to the public, allowing attackers to upload malicious tools or modify those already used by agents.
Vulnerability: Public cloud storage without controls
Impact: Agent takeover, remote code execution
Detection: Enable AWS CloudTrail or logging to monitor changes in buckets and unexpected file uploads
Remediation: Use S3 bucket policies to block public write/read; enable versioning; monitor access logs

instruction: Describe the Path Traversal attack: Directory Traversal in Document Loader
output:
AI agents that let users upload and read documents sometimes fail to validate file paths, allowing attackers to access sensitive files like passwords or config files.
Vulnerability: Improper input validation for file paths
Impact: Server info leak, credential exposure
Detection: Monitor logs for suspicious file access patterns (../, ..\\); validate paths server-side
Remediation: Always sanitize and validate user-provided paths; never allow raw path access from user input

instruction: Describe the Web Exploit attack: Weak CORS / CSRF Protection in LLM Apps
output:
LLM-based web apps often embed AI interfaces in browsers. If CORS or CSRF protections are weak, malicious sites can interact with the AI agent via user’s session.
Vulnerability: Poor CSRF/CORS protection
Impact: Silent data leaks, account hijack
Detection: Inspect referrer/origin headers, monitor unusual AI usage patterns
Remediation: Add CSRF tokens, enforce strict CORS, set SameSite=Strict/HTTPOnly cookies

instruction: Describe the SSRF / Fetch Abuse attack: LLM Agent Executing External URLs (No Filter)
output:
LLM plugins or agents often use tools like requests.get() to fetch URLs. Without filtering, attackers can trigger them to access internal servers or private files.
Vulnerability: No input filtering for fetch/requests
Impact: Internal data exposure, metadata leak
Detection: Monitor fetch requests; flag local IPs and metadata URLs in LLM plugin logs
Remediation: Use URL filtering, allowlists; block local IP ranges; sandbox LLM plugins

instruction: Describe the Model Theft attack: Unauthorized Access to Model Weights (ONNX, TFLite)
output:
AI models like ONNX, TFLite, or .pt are sometimes publicly exposed in apps. Attackers can download them, reverse-engineer, or steal proprietary models.
Vulnerability: Exposed or unprotected model files
Impact: IP theft, cloning, reverse engineering
Detection: Monitor cloud storage/public URLs for exposed .onnx or .tflite; use app store scanning
Remediation: Encrypt model files; use model wrappers; serve models via authenticated APIs

instruction: Describe the Container Abuse attack: Insecure Dockerfile with Exposed Ports
output:
A Dockerfile used to build an app image exposes critical ports (like 5000, 8000) to the internet without restriction.
Vulnerability: Open ports, unauthenticated access
Impact: Remote Code Execution, Data Exposure
Detection: Monitor open ports using security groups or firewalls; scan with Nmap and block unnecessary exposed ports
Remediation: Never expose internal ports to public; enforce firewall rules; always use authentication on dev ports

instruction: Describe the Secret Leak attack: Secrets in Code or Prompt Templates
output:
Developers accidentally embed hardcoded API keys, passwords, or tokens directly into prompt templates or code.
Vulnerability: Secrets hardcoded in code or templates
Impact: Unauthorized access, data leak
Detection: Use GitHub token scanning; monitor for unusual usage spikes
Remediation: Store secrets in environment variables or secure vaults; never hardcode keys in templates or code

instruction: Describe the CORS Misconfiguration attack: Allowing All Origins in LangChain Web UI
output:
LangChain web app allows all domains (*) in CORS headers, making it vulnerable to malicious site interactions.
Vulnerability: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
Impact: Credential theft, data exfiltration
Detection: Use browser security tools or ZAP to test CORS responses
Remediation: Never allow * for CORS in production; restrict origins strictly; enforce token-based auth for APIs

instruction: Describe the Info Disclosure attack: Verbose Error Messages in Agent Tools
output:
LLM-based or LangChain-based agent tools display detailed error messages (stack traces) that reveal internal details.
Vulnerability: Debug stack trace with sensitive info
Impact: Intelligence gathering, secondary attack setup
Detection: Monitor logs for excessive error responses; track repeated failed inputs
Remediation: Disable detailed errors in production; return generic error messages; log stack traces internally only

instruction: Describe the Denial of Service (DoS) attack: API Gateway with No Rate Limit
output:
LLM API backend has no request throttling, allowing attackers to overload it or increase cloud costs.
Vulnerability: No rate limit or quota control
Impact: API outage, billing abuse
Detection: Monitor traffic spikes, track IP patterns; set alerts for excessive token usage
Remediation: Enforce rate limits per user/IP; add global quota policies; use Cloudflare or AWS WAF to mitigate flood

instruction: Describe the Privilege Misuse attack: No IAM Policy on Agent-Calling Cloud APIs
output:
Agent (e.g., chatbot, plugin) runs with full cloud access instead of scoped permissions, enabling data theft.
Vulnerability: Overly permissive IAM roles
Impact: Cloud resource abuse, data exfiltration
Detection: Monitor IAM usage logs; review all roles granted to agent accounts
Remediation: Enforce least-privilege roles; regularly audit IAM permissions; use service boundaries in cloud projects

instruction: Describe the Temp File Race / RCE attack: Insecure Temp File Access by Agent Tools
output:
Agent tools use /tmp or temp folders without locking, allowing attackers to hijack file paths.
Vulnerability: Unlocked temp file usage
Impact: File hijack, data leak, privilege escalation
Detection: Monitor /tmp for race conditions; review file creation logs
Remediation: Use secure, unique file names with 600 permissions; delete temp files immediately after use

instruction: Describe the Credential Exposure attack: Hardcoded Admin Credentials in Localhost Agent
output:
Developer embeds admin username and password directly in source code or config → attacker accesses via logs or reverse.
Vulnerability: Hardcoded credentials in source
Impact: Full agent takeover, data access
Detection: Scan source repos and memory for hardcoded credentials
Remediation: Use environment variables; apply local auth with rotating credentials or tokens

instruction: Describe the Proxy Abuse / Misconfig attack: Port Forwarding Exploits on Remote Agent Setup
output:
Developers expose localhost services like http://127.0.0.1:5000 but mistakenly forward them to the public via SSH.
Vulnerability: Exposed localhost service to public
Impact: Full agent hijack, command execution
Detection: Monitor cloud egress and unusual incoming connections from tunnels
Remediation: Never forward localhost ports publicly without auth; require HTTPS + API keys or VPN

instruction: Describe the Secret Hygiene Failure attack: Improper Secret Rotation for API Keys
output:
Once API keys are leaked or exposed, they continue working indefinitely due to lack of rotation or monitoring.
Vulnerability: No secret expiration or validation
Impact: Key theft, API abuse, unexpected billing
Detection: Check billing dashboards; scan commits and config files for credentials
Remediation: Rotate keys periodically; use vault tools; monitor for exposure using GitHub secrets scanning

instruction: Describe the Unencrypted Traffic attack: No HTTPS on LLM Endpoint
output:
AI backend is served over HTTP instead of HTTPS, exposing all traffic (including credentials) to eavesdropping.
Vulnerability: No HTTPS (SSL/TLS) encryption
Impact: Credential theft, session hijack, data exposure
Detection: Use traffic inspection tools; check for http:// instead of https:// in config files
Remediation: Always enable HTTPS using free SSL (Let’s Encrypt); redirect all HTTP requests to HTTPS automatically

instruction: Describe the Remote RCE (Code Exec) attack: Debug Mode Enabled in Prod (e.g., Flask, FastAPI)
output:
Developer forgets to disable debug=True in Flask/FastAPI app, exposing an interactive shell to the internet, allowing anyone to run Python code.
Vulnerability: Debug shell exposed on production
Impact: Remote Code Execution, Server Compromise
Detection: Monitor for public debug endpoints, scan cloud with Shodan, use logging for traceback console usage
Remediation: Disable debug=True in production; use app.run(debug=False); restrict IP binding; deploy via Gunicorn or HTTPS proxy

instruction: Describe the Shell Injection attack: Agent Tool with os.system() in Logic
output:
LLM or plugin tool uses os.system() or subprocess without validation, allowing attacker to craft prompt that runs system-level commands.
Vulnerability: Unvalidated shell execution from user input
Impact: Full system takeover, data exfiltration
Detection: Monitor agent logs for dangerous shell commands; use prompt filtering
Remediation: Avoid os.system() in tools; use secure APIs; validate and sanitize user input strictly

instruction: Describe the Prompt Poisoning attack: RAG Context Injection from Shared Storage
output:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) agents load context from shared cloud storage (like S3), which can be poisoned to influence LLM outputs.
Vulnerability: Untrusted source for RAG context documents
Impact: Prompt injection, logic hijack, data leak
Detection: Monitor document updates in shared storage; compare vector index embeddings to known docs
Remediation: Restrict write access to RAG sources; scan context docs for prompt injection strings

instruction: Describe the Privilege Escalation attack: LLM Orchestrator Running as Root
output:
An AI orchestrator or LangChain/agent server is run with root/admin privileges. If any vulnerability is exploited, attacker gains full system control.
Vulnerability: Cloud VMs, LLM servers
Impact: T1068 – Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
Detection: Full server takeover via single agent exploit
Remediation: Check for agent user privileges; use monitoring tools like auditd or OSQuery

instruction: Describe the Recon / Data Exfiltration attack: Public Crawlers Can Access Agent Workspaces
output:
Developers expose their agent's workspaces or document roots to the internet without access control. Search engines index private data.
Vulnerability: Lack of file access control or crawler rules
Impact: Information leakage, privacy violation
Detection: Use Google Search Console to check indexed files; scan site using tools like Screaming Frog
Remediation: Add robots.txt to block crawlers; protect /uploads/, /logs/, /docs/ folders with auth or private cloud buckets

instruction: Describe the Input Injection / Function Abuse attack: No Input Validation in Function-Calling Tool
output:
LangChain or plugin tool takes user input and passes it directly to function calls like file access, shell tools, or APIs — attacker can inject dangerous values.
Vulnerability: Missing input sanitization or restrictions
Impact: Arbitrary file access or function abuse
Detection: Log and review all user inputs; enforce argument types and validation at function level
Remediation: Use input validators (e.g., pydantic); never let LLM construct raw file paths or command strings

instruction: Describe the Privilege Escalation attack: LLM Orchestrator Running as Root
output:
An AI orchestrator or LangChain/agent server is run with root/admin privileges. If any vulnerability is exploited, attacker gains full system control.
Vulnerability: Cloud VMs, LLM servers
Impact: T1068 – Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
Detection: Full server takeover via single agent exploit
Remediation: Check for agent user privileges; use monitoring tools like auditd or OSQuery

instruction: Describe the Recon / Data Exfiltration attack: Public Crawlers Can Access Agent Workspaces
output:
Developers expose their agent's workspaces or document roots to the internet without access control. Search engines index private data.
Vulnerability: Lack of file access control or crawler rules
Impact: Information leakage, privacy violation
Detection: Use Google Search Console to check indexed files; scan site using tools like Screaming Frog
Remediation: Add robots.txt to block crawlers; protect /uploads/, /logs/, /docs/ folders with auth or private cloud buckets

instruction: Describe the Input Injection / Function Abuse attack: No Input Validation in Function-Calling Tool
output:
LangChain or plugin tool takes user input and passes it directly to function calls like file access, shell tools, or APIs — attacker can inject dangerous values.
Vulnerability: Missing input sanitization or restrictions
Impact: Arbitrary file access or function abuse
Detection: Log and review all user inputs; enforce argument types and validation at function level
Remediation: Use input validators (e.g., pydantic); never let LLM construct raw file paths or command strings

instruction: Describe the Privilege Escalation via API attack: Overprivileged API Key Usage
output:
An application uses an API key with too many permissions (more than it needs). If the key is leaked, an attacker can use it to access or damage services.
Vulnerability: Too much access granted to API key
Impact: Account Takeover, Data Exfiltration
Detection: Scan codebase for secrets; review cloud logs for key usage; use tools like AWS CloudTrail to detect unusual behavior
Remediation: Use least privilege on all API keys; rotate keys regularly; apply service boundaries, IP restrictions, and monitoring

instruction: Describe the Credential Leakage via Source Code attack: Hardcoded Credentials in LLM Tooling
output:
Developers often embed API keys or passwords directly into LLM scripts or tools for convenience. If these are exposed (e.g., via GitHub or logs), attackers can misuse them.
Vulnerability: Hardcoded secrets in source code
Impact: API abuse, data theft, cost spike
Detection: Monitor GitHub commits; scan for secrets with TruffleHog/Gitleaks; monitor LLM API usage for anomalies
Remediation: Use environment variables or secret managers (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager); never commit secrets to code

instruction: Describe the Credential Stuffing / Brute Force via Login Form attack: Password Brute Force on Web Login Forms
output:
A malicious actor attempts to gain unauthorized access to user accounts by systematically guessing passwords on a login form using either dictionary or pure brute force attack methods. This is done via automation or scripts.
Vulnerability: Weak login rate-limiting, no CAPTCHA, guessable credentials
Impact: Unauthorized access, data theft, account takeover
Detection: Monitor login attempts per IP/user; detect excessive login failures
Remediation: Enforce rate-limiting; CAPTCHA; multi-factor auth; use strong passwords; lockout after N attempts

instruction: Describe the Online Password Guessing attack: Dictionary Attack on Login Forms
output:
The attacker uses a list of commonly used passwords (a dictionary) and systematically tries each one against a known username on a login form. Unlike brute force, this is limited to realistic password guesses rather than every possible combination.
Vulnerability: Weak password policy, no login rate-limiting
Impact: Account takeover, unauthorized access
Detection: Monitor failed login attempts; detect excessive login failures per IP/user
Remediation: Enforce strong passwords, use rate-limiting, CAPTCHA, and account lockout after N failures

instruction: Describe the Offline Hash Cracking Using Brute Force attack: Hash Brute Forcing (Offline Cracking)
output:
Attackers obtain leaked or dumped password hashes from a breached database and try to crack them offline using brute force techniques to recover the original plaintext password. This attack doesn't interact with the application directly.
Vulnerability: Weak or unsalted password hashes
Impact: Password exposure, credential reuse on other systems
Detection: Monitor for leaked hashes on forums; analyze hash storage technique; enable canary token traps
Remediation: Salted and hashed passwords using bcrypt/scrypt/argon2; avoid storing weak or unhashed passwords

instruction: Describe the Network Protocol Brute Force (Remote Shell Access) attack: SSH Brute Force Attack
output:
Attackers try many username and password combinations to gain unauthorized SSH access to a server, using brute force over port 22. Often done against internet-exposed servers with default or weak credentials.
Vulnerability: Exposed SSH with weak credentials
Impact: Full system access, server takeover
Detection: Monitor /var/log/auth.log, enable Fail2Ban, alert on excessive login failures from same IP
Remediation: Disable root login, enforce key-based auth, rate-limit SSH, block repeated IPs via Fail2Ban

instruction: Describe the HTTP Authentication Brute Forcing attack: HTTP Basic Auth Brute Force
output:
HTTP Basic Authentication prompts for a username/password in the browser. Attackers can brute-force this using automated tools by sending Base64-encoded credentials to the endpoint repeatedly until valid credentials are found.
Vulnerability: No rate limiting, no MFA, guessable credentials
Impact: Unauthorized access to internal systems
Detection: Monitor access logs for repeated Base64 login attempts; alert on brute-force behavior
Remediation: Use digest or token-based auth, add rate-limiting, implement 2FA

instruction: Describe the API Token / Key Guessing attack: API Key or Token Brute Force
output:
APIs using static tokens (e.g., ?api_key=XYZ) or bearer tokens in headers can be brute-forced if poorly designed. Attackers attempt many keys to guess a valid one and access protected endpoints.
Vulnerability: Predictable or static API tokens
Impact: Unauthorized API access, data exposure
Detection: Monitor failed token use per IP/user-agent; log unusual key lengths or formats
Remediation: Use rate-limiting, expire keys, use longer random tokens, monitor access per key

instruction: Describe the CAPTCHA Weakness Exploitation via Automation attack: CAPTCHA Bypass via Brute Force
output:
Attackers attempt to bypass CAPTCHAs by automating form submissions, using OCR, guessing static challenges, or exploiting logic flaws to continue brute force attacks even when CAPTCHA is present.
Vulnerability: Weak or broken CAPTCHA logic
Impact: Enables further brute force or spam attacks
Detection: Analyze form behavior; monitor for repeated CAPTCHA failures with same IP or timing
Remediation: Use modern CAPTCHA (reCAPTCHA v3+); implement rate-limiting even on correct CAPTCHA; log anomaly patterns

instruction: Describe the Keyspace Exhaustion / Symmetric Key Cracking attack: Brute Forcing Cryptographic Keys
output:
Attackers try all possible key combinations to decrypt data encrypted with weak algorithms (e.g., 56-bit DES or short AES keys). This is a pure cryptographic brute-force attack done offline.
Vulnerability: Weak encryption or short keys used
Impact: Full decryption of confidential data
Detection: Monitor encrypted file access; check for high CPU/GPU usage indicating key attempts
Remediation: Use strong encryption (AES-256+); never use DES/3DES; enforce long, random keys

instruction: Describe the Resource Discovery via Forced Browsing attack: Directory or File Name Brute Forcing
output:
Attackers attempt to discover hidden files, admin panels, config files, or unlisted pages on a web server by brute-forcing common paths or filenames (like /admin, /backup.zip, /test.php, etc.)
Vulnerability: Accessible but unlinked files/folders
Impact: Information leakage, sensitive file exposure
Detection: Monitor for high volume 404s; use WAFs to detect scanning
Remediation: Use .htaccess, remove sensitive files, monitor access logs, hide backup/config endpoints

instruction: Describe the DNS Enumeration via Brute Force attack: Subdomain Brute Force
output:
Attackers discover subdomains (e.g., admin.target.com, dev.target.com) by trying many common names to see which resolve via DNS. These subdomains may expose internal tools, staging servers, or forgotten deployments.
Vulnerability: Forgotten or exposed subdomains
Impact: Exposure of dev portals, admin sites, or internal apps
Detection: Monitor DNS logs or external recon scans from passive sources
Remediation: Use wildcard DNS + monitoring; limit exposed subdomains; regularly audit DNS records

instruction: Describe the CAPTCHA Token Prediction or Reuse attack: CAPTCHA Token Guessing
output:
Attackers guess or reuse CAPTCHA tokens to bypass form protections, especially when the token is predictable, static, or weakly implemented (e.g., timestamp-based, session-based, or sent in hidden fields).
Vulnerability: Predictable or static CAPTCHA tokens
Impact: CAPTCHA bypass → brute force, spam, abuse
Detection: Check for token reuse, short token formats, token lifetimes
Remediation: Use encrypted tokens, server-side validation, expiry, strong randomness

instruction: Describe the Session Hijacking via Predictable IDs attack: Session ID Brute Forcing
output:
Attackers try to guess or brute-force session IDs to hijack valid user sessions. If session tokens are short, predictable, or improperly implemented (e.g., incremental IDs or encoded usernames), attackers can impersonate users.
Vulnerability: Weak/random session token generation
Impact: Unauthorized access, identity theft
Detection: Monitor session anomalies (IP changes, reuse patterns); analyze token entropy
Remediation: Use long, random, cryptographically strong session IDs; tie to IP/device; invalidate on logout

instruction: Describe the OTP/2FA Brute Forcing via Code Guessing attack: Multi-Factor Code Brute Force
output:
Attackers attempt to guess Time-Based One-Time Passwords (TOTPs) or codes sent via email/SMS in 2FA-enabled systems. This is possible when there is no rate-limiting or lockout on repeated OTP attempts.
Vulnerability: No rate-limiting or CAPTCHA on OTP/2FA
Impact: Full 2FA bypass and account compromise
Detection: Monitor OTP failures per IP/device; detect too many attempts on OTP/2FA endpoints
Remediation: Enforce lockout after N wrong OTPs, use CAPTCHAs, restrict IPs, use TOTP with strict expiration

instruction: Describe the File Inclusion/Guessing via Path Brute Force attack: Local File Brute Force in Web Apps
output:
Attackers attempt to discover and access local files in a web app (e.g., config.php, .env, backup.bak) by guessing or brute-forcing file names and inclusion parameters. These may expose credentials or source code.
Vulnerability: Unvalidated file paths or accessible sensitive files
Impact: Exposure of credentials, DB info, source code
