Impact: Stealth malware delivery
Detection: Web gateway logs, JS analysis in email content
Remediation: Block JS rendering in email clients

instruction: Describe the VBS File via Email attack: VBS-based Keylogger via Email
output:
Attacker delivers a VBS file disguised as a secure login tool. When executed, it installs a keylogger and sends keystrokes to the attacker.
Vulnerability: Scripting engines enabled, no attachment filtering
Impact: Continuous credential theft
Detection: EDR monitoring script execution, strange email traffic
Remediation: Disable VBS, email content inspection

instruction: Describe the JS via PDF Email Attachment attack: Embedded JS Downloader in PDF
output:
PDF contains embedded JavaScript that launches an external URL to download malware silently. Email tricks victim into opening the PDF.
Vulnerability: PDF JS execution enabled, URL filters weak
Impact: Malware delivery, initial access
Detection: Proxy logs, PDF sandboxing, AV alerts
Remediation: Disable JS in PDF readers, isolate PDF opening

instruction: Describe the HTA File as Chat File attack: Fake Chat Transcript HTA Dropper
output:
A fake support transcript (e.g., from “Tech Support”) is delivered via HTA file. Executing it deploys a backdoor and opens Notepad as a decoy.
Vulnerability: Trust in support files, no mshta control
Impact: Persistent remote access
Detection: EDR, netstat, PowerShell telemetry
Remediation: Block mshta, restrict outbound PowerShell

instruction: Describe the JS File Obfuscation in Attachment attack: Obfuscated JavaScript Order Form
output:
The attacker sends a .js file named as an “order form” but obfuscated using JS packers. It deploys malware silently.
Vulnerability: JS execution allowed, social engineering
Impact: Initial foothold, lateral movement
Detection: Static code analysis, proxy logs
Remediation: Restrict script file types, user training

instruction: Describe the HTA Linked in Signature attack: HTA Script via Email Signature Link
output:
Malicious HTA file hosted online is linked inside a fake company signature. Victim clicks thinking it's a business profile.
Vulnerability: Trust in signatures, mshta.exe active
Impact: Remote shell access
Detection: Link monitoring, mshta.exe tracking
Remediation: Disable HTA, alert on link shorteners

instruction: Describe the VBS Inside EXE Archive attack: Malicious Script in Self-Extracting Archive
output:
VBS script hidden inside a .exe self-extracting archive sent as an "installer" or "patch". Executing it drops and runs malware.
Vulnerability: Lack of sandboxing, trust in patches
Impact: Initial malware drop
Detection: Heuristics for SFX archives, user behavior
Remediation: Block EXEs in email, restrict SFX behavior

instruction: Describe the JS Encrypted ZIP attack: JavaScript Exploit via Encrypted Attachment
output:
Malicious JavaScript file sent inside a password-protected ZIP to bypass AV scanning. Victim is given password in the email.
Vulnerability: AV cannot scan encrypted ZIPs
Impact: Credential exfiltration
Detection: Monitor JS execution, ZIP attachment usage
Remediation: Block encrypted ZIPs, educate staff

instruction: Describe the HTA Masquerade attack: HTA File Masked as PDF
output:
HTA file renamed to “filename.pdf.hta” and disguised with a PDF icon. Users fooled into thinking it’s a regular document.
Vulnerability: Extension spoofing, icon manipulation
Impact: Remote access
Detection: File extension filter, sandbox testing
Remediation: Show extensions, block HTA

instruction: Describe the JS with Registry Persistence attack: Multi-Stage JS Downloader with Persistence
output:
JavaScript script delivered that not only downloads malware but also modifies registry to persist after reboot.
Vulnerability: Startup persistence allowed, JS execution
Impact: Long-term infection
Detection: Registry changes logs, EDR startup script alerts
Remediation: Disable Run key, restrict scripts

instruction: Describe the VBS with Dual Extension attack: VBS File Camouflaged as TXT
output:
A file named “ShippingInfo.txt.vbs” is sent via email, pretending to be a text document. Users with hidden extensions enabled are tricked.
Vulnerability: Hidden extensions, trust in .txt files
Impact: System compromise
Detection: File extension logging, user behavior monitoring
Remediation: Show full extensions, block VBS

instruction: Describe the HTA Embedded in ICS Calendar attack: HTA Dropper from Email Calendar Invite
output:
HTA payload embedded in an ICS calendar invite attachment. When opened in Outlook, victim downloads and runs HTA file via calendar link.
Vulnerability: Calendar rendering linkable, mshta.exe enabled
Impact: Initial Access + Remote Control
Detection: Proxy logs, EDR detection on mshta.exe
Remediation: Sanitize ICS, block mshta.exe

instruction: Describe the VBS Masquerading as Viewer attack: Fake Document Viewer in VBS
output:
Attacker sends a "Secure Document Viewer.vbs" file that runs malware disguised as viewer software.
Vulnerability: Trust in tools, VBS allowed by OS
Impact: Stealth infection & user deception
Detection: WSH telemetry, AV behavior-based rules
Remediation: Block VBS, monitor execution of WScript

instruction: Describe the JS via Shared Link Email attack: Malicious JS in Shared Google Drive Notification
output:
Attacker shares a Google Drive-hosted JS file and sends Google’s share notification email, abusing trusted domain.
Vulnerability: Blind trust in cloud notifications
Impact: Delivery of initial payload
Detection: DNS/proxy logs, endpoint behavior
Remediation: Cloud link filtering, user awareness

instruction: Describe the HTML Attachment with Embedded HTA attack: HTA Loader as Email HTML Attachment
output:
Attacker embeds VBScript inside an HTML email attachment that extracts and launches HTA on click.
Vulnerability: HTML rendering, script execution in browser/email
Impact: Exploits local trust in HTML files
Detection: HTML inspection, HTA execution monitoring
Remediation: Disable scriptable objects in email clients

instruction: Describe the JS Activating MS Word via Shell attack: JS Script Triggering Word Macros
output:
A JavaScript file executes and uses Shell object to open a malicious Word file which has auto-macros.
Vulnerability: Word macros enabled, script access to shell
Impact: Layered payload chaining
Detection: App behavior logging, macro triggers
Remediation: Disable macros + script blocking

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling via Encrypted JavaScript Blob
output:
Attacker sends a seemingly safe email with an HTML attachment that constructs a malware file using JavaScript Blob inside the browser, bypassing traditional email security scanners.
Vulnerability: Email Clients Allow HTML Execution
Impact: Remote Code Execution, Initial Access
Detection: Monitor HTML attachments with JavaScript blobs or download triggers
Remediation: Disable script execution in HTML attachments; block .html attachments in emails

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling with Fake Job Offer
output:
A job seeker receives an email from a fake recruiter with an HTML file attached that creates a backdoor dropper using JavaScript and saves it to the system silently.
Vulnerability: Obfuscated JavaScript Execution in Email Attachment
Impact: Persistent Backdoor
Detection: Endpoint monitoring, track VBScript creation events
Remediation: Disable HTML attachments; train users not to open unsolicited recruiter attachments

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: Smuggling Payloads Using HTML Form Auto-Submission
output:
A malicious HTML file auto-submits a hidden form containing a malicious script to the user's browser, creating a weaponized downloader disguised as a document.
Vulnerability: No user confirmation for form execution in browser
Impact: File Encryption, Data Loss
Detection: Monitor .bat creation; browser sandboxing
Remediation: Warn users about unexpected attachments; disable auto form processing

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling via Download Link Generator
output:
The attacker sends an HTML file that generates a fake download button mimicking a secure document portal, but delivers malware disguised as PDF.
Vulnerability: Trust in filename extension and icon
Impact: Credential Theft
Detection: Monitor downloads with double extensions
Remediation: Block .html and .exe in mail server filters; train users

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling with Inline SVG + JavaScript
output:
Attacker hides JavaScript inside an inline SVG element in an HTML email attachment. The script reconstructs and drops a PowerShell script used to install spyware.
Vulnerability: Abuse of SVG scripting support
Impact: Surveillance, Data Theft
Detection: Monitor usage of mshta.exe and inline scripts
Remediation: Strip out SVG/script combo from HTML files in email

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling Using ZIP Loader and JavaScript Blob
output:
Attacker embeds JavaScript in HTML that reconstructs a ZIP file containing malware. The ZIP is downloaded silently and extracted by the user, tricking them into running malware.
Vulnerability: Browser allows Blob-based download
Impact: System Compromise
Detection: Monitor unexpected ZIP downloads from HTML
Remediation: Block encoded ZIP blobs in attachments

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling with Data URI Payload
output:
Payload is embedded directly in a data URI inside HTML, which runs immediately when opened.
Vulnerability: Data URI bypasses content filters
Impact: Silent Malware Installation
Detection: Inspect attachment for data URI + JavaScript
Remediation: Sanitize Data URI use in emails

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling in Password Reset Request Scam
output:
Email claims to be from IT requesting a password reset confirmation, with an attached HTML file containing a phishing payload that mimics SSO login.
Vulnerability: Local file executed in browser looks trusted
Impact: Credential Theft
Detection: Detect login forms in HTML attachments
Remediation: Strip login forms from inbound HTML files

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling with QR Code Bait
output:
HTML file renders a QR code which, when scanned, links to a malware-hosting site generated dynamically by JavaScript.
Vulnerability: Trust in QR code artifacts
Impact: Cross-device compromise
Detection: Monitor email attachments generating QR
Remediation: Disable active script + prevent QR abuse

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling via Resume Submission Email
output:
Fake applicant sends a resume email with an HTML attachment that drops an obfuscated .exe file.
Vulnerability: Lack of double-extension blocking
Impact: RAT Deployment
Detection: Scan attachments for dual extensions
Remediation: Enforce naming conventions & filters

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling with JavaScript Obfuscation Chain
output:
Attacker obfuscates JavaScript in layers so that security tools can’t detect payload. The file rebuilds a .js dropper.
Vulnerability: Anti-virus bypass via JS obfuscation
Impact: Data Exfiltration
Detection: Detect use of eval, atob, long unicode
Remediation: Block eval & suspicious JS patterns

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling via Embedded iframe to Malicious CDN
output:
HTML contains an iframe that silently pulls malicious script from CDN and runs it in user's browser.
Vulnerability: Trust in embedded web objects
Impact: Persistent Malware
Detection: Detect suspicious CDN calls in iframe
Remediation: Block iframe src in HTML email

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling via Auto-generated Excel Sheet
output:
The HTML simulates an Excel document interface in browser with fake macros that download malware.
Vulnerability: Familiar interface mimics Excel trust
Impact: Credential Capture
Detection: Monitor HTML UIs with click actions
Remediation: User education; block pseudo-Excel HTML

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling via External Script Injection
output:
The HTML file loads an external JavaScript payload dynamically via DOM manipulation and writes a dropper file.
Vulnerability: Trust in benign-looking HTML + remote code
Impact: Silent Infection
Detection: Monitor remote script inclusion
Remediation: Block dynamic <script> in HTML files

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling via SVG-Encoded PowerShell Script
output:
A PowerShell command is hidden inside SVG, loaded via HTML attachment and silently executed.
Vulnerability: SVG tag content overlooked by scanners
Impact: Remote Spyware
Detection: Scan SVG for non-visual tags
Remediation: Block SVG parsing inside HTML

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling with PDF-like Interface (Polyglot HTML)
output:
A highly convincing HTML attachment mimics a PDF viewer and tricks the user into clicking a fake "Print" button that downloads malware.
Vulnerability: Trust in PDF file appearance
Impact: Credential or financial data theft
Detection: Look for fake PDF UIs in HTML
Remediation: Strip or quarantine fake UI mimicry in mail filters

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling via Browser Cache Abuse
output:
Attacker uses HTML with JavaScript that loads malware in pieces from browser cache after receiving an email, bypassing file scanners.
Vulnerability: File scanner cannot scan browser cache
Impact: Scanner Evasion + Initial Compromise
Detection: Inspect cache access via HTML attachments
Remediation: Clear cache on session end; block cache-assembling scripts

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling via Clipboard Injection
output:
Attacker uses JavaScript in HTML to silently copy a PowerShell malware command to the user's clipboard when the file is opened.
Vulnerability: Clipboard abuse in browser not monitored
Impact: User-assisted Infection
Detection: Monitor clipboard events on file open
Remediation: Disable clipboard access for untrusted HTML

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling via Email Auto-Forward Rule
output:
Attack includes HTML that configures a hidden email auto-forward rule via Outlook scripting, leaking future emails to attacker.
Vulnerability: No prompts for new email rule creation
Impact: Email Surveillance
Detection: Monitor changes to Outlook rules
Remediation: Block Outlook rule creation from scripts

instruction: Describe the HTML Smuggling attack: HTML Smuggling Using Fake System Update Notice
output:
HTML displays a fake OS update screen inside the browser with progress bar. After a delay, it downloads malware disguised as update installer.
Vulnerability: Visual mimicry of OS update screens
Impact: User Deception & Backdoor Install
Detection: Block full-screen HTML attachments
Remediation: Educate users on real update processes

instruction: Describe the Brute Force attack: OWA Login Brute Force on Corporate Email
output:
Attacker targets a corporate Outlook Web App (OWA) portal using Hydra to brute-force employee credentials.
Vulnerability: Weak Password Policy, No Rate Limiting
Impact: Unauthorized access to employee inbox
Detection: Monitor login attempts per IP, look for many failed logins
Remediation: Enforce lockout after 5 failed logins, MFA, IP whitelisting

instruction: Describe the Password Spray attack: Gmail Account Takeover via Password Spray
output:
Attacker performs a password spray attack on personal Gmail accounts using a large email list and common passwords.
Vulnerability: Weak/common passwords reused
Impact: Compromised personal email, identity theft
Detection: Gmail alerts unusual sign-in activity; impossible travel alert
Remediation: Strong password policy, MFA enabled

instruction: Describe the Password Brute Force attack: Microsoft 365 Account Attack via Azure AD Endpoint
output:
Brute-force attack on Microsoft 365 user accounts via Azure login endpoints using scripting tools.
Vulnerability: Legacy authentication enabled, weak password
Impact: Unauthorized access to enterprise email & SharePoint
Detection: Excessive failed logins in Azure logs
Remediation: Disable legacy auth, conditional access policy, enforce MFA

instruction: Describe the IMAP Brute Force attack: IMAP Brute Force via Hydra Against cPanel Mail
output:
Brute-force attack targets a hosting provider's mail server using IMAP protocol on port 993.
Vulnerability: IMAP access open, weak auth controls
Impact: Full access to mail account, data leak
Detection: Anomalous IMAP login patterns
Remediation: Disable IMAP or rate-limit logins

instruction: Describe the SMTP Password Attack attack: SMTP Auth Brute Force to Hijack Email Sending
output:
Attacker brute-forces SMTP AUTH to send phishing/spam from compromised accounts.
Vulnerability: SMTP auth with weak creds, open relay
Impact: Hijack of email account, spam/phishing sent
Detection: Monitor SMTP logs and spam complaints
Remediation: Use DKIM/DMARC/SPF, enforce strong auth

instruction: Describe the Password Spray attack: Password Spray Attack on Roundcube Webmail
output:
Attacker targets Roundcube email portal used by a university by spraying common passwords across many known usernames.
Vulnerability: Default credentials reused, no MFA
Impact: Unauthorized access to student or staff emails
Detection: Excessive login failures from a single IP
Remediation: MFA + lockout policies + CAPTCHA

instruction: Describe the Password Spray attack: VoIP Email Portal Spray Attack
output:
A VoIP service uses email-based login for voicemail, which is targeted using password spray to access recordings.
Vulnerability: Predictable passwords, no CAPTCHA
Impact: Eavesdropping on internal messages
Detection: Logins from new IPs, access to voicemail logs
Remediation: Complex password rules + monitoring

instruction: Describe the Brute Force attack: Zimbra Webmail Brute Force
output:
Zimbra mail server login targeted using brute-force attack via dictionary-based tool.
Vulnerability: Default creds, brute-forceable endpoint
Impact: Admin email compromise
Detection: Too many POST failures from a client
Remediation: Lockout per user + proxy detection

instruction: Describe the Password Spray attack: Office365 Legacy IMAP Spray Attack
output:
Attacker bypasses modern MFA by spraying legacy IMAP login across Office365 accounts.
Vulnerability: Legacy auth bypasses MFA
Impact: Email access, MFA bypass
Detection: Logs show legacy protocol use
Remediation: Disable IMAP, enforce modern auth only

instruction: Describe the Brute Force attack: Shared Mailbox Brute Force in Enterprise
output:
Attacker brute-forces credentials of a shared mailbox account used for HR queries (e.g., hr@company.com).
Vulnerability: No lockout policy for shared inbox
Impact: Sensitive HR info leak
Detection: Detect multiple failures to shared accounts
Remediation: Separate auth for shared boxes + strong policy

instruction: Describe the Password Brute Force attack: Apple Mail (iCloud) Brute Force via IMAP
output:
Attacker targets iCloud mail using automated IMAP login attempts.
Vulnerability: Weak password reuse
Impact: Access to financial receipts, PII
Detection: Apple alerts suspicious logins
Remediation: Strong password + iCloud MFA

instruction: Describe the Brute Force attack: SMTP AUTH Brute Force for Sending Internal Spam
output:
Attack brute-forces SMTP auth on port 587 to send phishing from internal IP.
Vulnerability: SMTP open for auth externally
Impact: Spam from inside domain, brand damage
Detection: SPF/DKIM failure alerts, bounce logs
Remediation: Rate limit SMTP logins, enforce 2FA

instruction: Describe the API Brute Force attack: Brute Forcing Email via Mobile App API
output:
Mobile email client API endpoint targeted with credential brute force.
Vulnerability: Weak rate-limiting on mobile APIs
Impact: Unauthorized access from mobile vector
Detection: API abuse alerts, login anomalies
Remediation: Rate-limiting + device fingerprinting

instruction: Describe the Credential Stuffing attack: Email Credential Stuffing from Breach Dump
output:
Attacker reuses email-password pairs from a public data breach on new email portals.
Vulnerability: Credential reuse
Impact: Large-scale takeover from reuse
Detection: Impossible login location alert
Remediation: Enforce unique passwords, MFA

instruction: Describe the Botnet Distributed Brute Force attack: Office365 Brute Force via SMTP Auth from Botnet
output:
Distributed brute-force SMTP auth on O365 from hundreds of bot IPs to avoid detection.
Vulnerability: No geo/IP detection, SMTP auth open
Impact: Widespread compromise, undetected by single-IP defense
Detection: Volume-based SMTP logs, UEBA alerts
Remediation: Geo-fencing, SMTP auth throttling

instruction: Describe the SMTP Password Brute Force attack: Brute-Force on Exim Mail Server via SMTP Login
output:
An attacker targets an Exim SMTP server (used on Linux servers) by brute-forcing login credentials to send emails as a legitimate user.
Vulnerability: SMTP authentication exposed externally
Impact: Attacker gains ability to send spoofed internal emails
Detection: Log monitoring, spam filter alerts, volume anomalies
Remediation: Limit external SMTP access, enforce strong passwords

instruction: Describe the POP3 Brute Force attack: Brute Force on Yahoo Mail via POP3 Legacy Access
output:
Attacker targets legacy POP3 access on Yahoo Mail using credential guessing for unauthorized mailbox access.
Vulnerability: POP3 legacy enabled, weak password reuse
Impact: Full inbox compromise without triggering MFA
Detection: Yahoo security alerts, access from new location/IP
Remediation: Disable legacy POP3 access, enforce OAuth/MFA

instruction: Describe the Brute Force attack: Webmail Brute Force on Horde Email Client
output:
Attacker targets Horde webmail login page by brute-forcing user credentials to access web interface and stored messages.
Vulnerability: Weak authentication, no CAPTCHA
Impact: User email compromise, data leak
Detection: High login failures in access logs
Remediation: CAPTCHA, login delay, MFA

instruction: Describe the Password Spray attack: Targeted Password Spray on Medical Staff Email Portal
output:
Attacker targets hospital staff login portal using a limited number of passwords across many user accounts to avoid lockout.
Vulnerability: No MFA, predictable passwords
Impact: Access to sensitive health records, HIPAA violation
Detection: Excessive failed login attempts
Remediation: MFA, IP-based lockout, breach monitoring

instruction: Describe the Password Spray attack: Microsoft Exchange Password Spray via RPC over HTTP
output:
Attacker targets Exchange RPC login endpoint using a known list of employees and predictable password formats.
Vulnerability: Legacy protocol, no MFA for Outlook
Impact: Silent takeover, financial theft, insider spying
Detection: OWA logs show failed RPC logins
Remediation: Modern auth enforcement, email rules monitoring

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: SMTP Packet Capture & Replay
output:
Attacker captures SMTP packets using a network sniffer and replays them to impersonate a user and resend sensitive emails.
Vulnerability: Unencrypted SMTP over LAN
Impact: Replay of confidential information, impersonation
Detection: Monitor duplicate email IDs, analyze headers
Remediation: Use STARTTLS, enforce secure SMTP with authentication

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: Replay Attack Using Captured SMTP Credentials
output:
SMTP credentials captured from earlier sniffed traffic are used to resend previous emails or spam.
Vulnerability: Weak Authentication, Lack of Encryption
Impact: Spoofing, spam injection, unauthorized access
Detection: Email log monitoring, header analysis
Remediation: Use TLS encryption, disable plaintext auth

instruction: Describe the Message Interception attack: Man-in-the-Middle Replay via Rogue Wi-Fi
output:
Attacker creates a rogue access point, intercepts SMTP traffic, and resends it with altered content.
Vulnerability: No SSL, Rogue AP, Unencrypted SMTP
Impact: Financial fraud, trust abuse, man-in-the-middle
Detection: Detect rogue SSIDs, check DKIM/headers
Remediation: Use TLS/SSL SMTP, implement SPF/DKIM

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: Message Replay via Internal Email Server Logs
output:
Insider replays previously sent emails by accessing raw SMTP logs on internal servers.
Vulnerability: Insider Access, Log Exposure
Impact: Data leakage, false communication
Detection: Enable alerting for duplicate headers
Remediation: Restrict log access, monitor insider behavior

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: SMTP Replay via Delayed Delivery Exploit
output:
Attacker crafts SMTP messages with delayed delivery and re-sends them repeatedly to flood or confuse recipient.
Vulnerability: Header Manipulation, SMTP Replay
Impact: Confusion, spam, trust exploitation
Detection: Compare timestamps & headers
Remediation: Block repeated delivery attempts via filters

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: SMTP Replay via Compromised Mail Archive
output:
Attacker gains access to a backup or archive of sent emails, extracts original messages, and replays them via SMTP to impersonate user.
Vulnerability: Backup exposure, mail archives
Impact: Message replay, impersonation
Detection: Unusual timestamp patterns
Remediation: Encrypt backups, restrict mail archive access

instruction: Describe the Message Interception attack: Intercepted SMTP via Public Proxy
output:
Email client misconfigured to use a public SMTP relay; attacker uses proxy logs to capture and replay messages.
Vulnerability: Misconfigured open SMTP relays
Impact: Confidential data leakage
Detection: Analyze open relay logs
Remediation: Avoid public proxies, use authenticated SMTP only

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: SMTP Replay through Internal Compromised Router
output:
A compromised router inside the network captures SMTP traffic and enables replay of confidential emails.
Vulnerability: Internal router compromise
Impact: Message replication, credential leak
Detection: Monitor router behavior
Remediation: Harden routers, restrict packet capture

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: SMTP Replay via DNS Hijack
output:
Attacker hijacks victim’s DNS, redirects SMTP connection to a rogue mail server to intercept and replay messages.
Vulnerability: DNS hijacking, no DNSSEC
Impact: Message tampering, phishing injection
Detection: Unusual routing or server IPs
Remediation: Use DNSSEC, validate SMTP certificates

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: SMTP Replay via Credential Stuffing
output:
Using stolen credentials from breaches, attacker logs into real SMTP servers and resends prior emails.
Vulnerability: Password reuse, exposed credentials
Impact: Account takeover, malicious replay
Detection: Detect login from new geolocation
Remediation: Use MFA, monitor failed SMTP auth attempts

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: SMTP Replay via Client-Side Script Injection
output:
Attacker exploits vulnerable webmail client to inject a script that auto-resends specific messages.
Vulnerability: Stored XSS in webmail
Impact: Stealth replay, exfiltration
Detection: CSP headers, check outbox anomalies
Remediation: Patch XSS, enable CSP and sandbox iframes

instruction: Describe the Message Interception attack: SMTP Replay via MX Record Poisoning
output:
Attacker poisons DNS MX records to route outgoing email through rogue SMTP server.
Vulnerability: MX poisoning, DNS tampering
Impact: Data interception, message hijack
Detection: Verify MX integrity, DNS monitoring
Remediation: Secure DNS using DNSSEC and split-DNS

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: SMTP Replay via Email Forwarding Rule Abuse
output:
Attacker sets up forwarding rules to intercept and later resend confidential emails.
Vulnerability: Unrestricted forwarding
Impact: Insider replay, impersonation
Detection: Check forwarding rules
Remediation: Restrict forwarding externally, alert admins

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: SMTP Replay via Shared Mailbox Abuse
output:
Legitimate users with access to a shared mailbox use its sent items to replay or modify old emails.
Vulnerability: Lack of user monitoring
Impact: Social engineering, replay spoofing
Detection: Monitor sent items activity
Remediation: Audit mailbox access logs

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: Replay via SMTP Open Relay Abuse
output:
Attacker uses misconfigured open SMTP relay to send replayed messages without auth.
Vulnerability: Open relay misconfig
Impact: Spam replay, phishing, impersonation
Detection: Detect open relays on network
Remediation: Block relays, enable SMTP auth

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: Replay via Outbox Sync Hijack
output:
Attacker gains access to an email client’s unsent or queued messages and replays them by syncing to a forged SMTP endpoint.
Vulnerability: SMTP endpoint hijack
Impact: Message theft, replay without detection
Detection: Compare email client Outbox vs Sent Items
Remediation: Encrypt drafts, restrict local access

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: Replay via SMTP “Resend” Function Abuse
output:
Some email clients have a “Resend” or “Send Again” function that can be exploited to replicate old messages with minimal effort.
Vulnerability: Abuse of client features
Impact: Easy message cloning, social engineering
Detection: Monitor repeat subjects with exact body match
Remediation: Log client-level resend actions

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: Replay via SMTP Logging on Misconfigured Server
output:
SMTP servers with verbose logging enabled store entire emails in plaintext, which an attacker with access can replay.
Vulnerability: Verbose logging exposure
Impact: Unauthorized message resend
Detection: Disable verbose mail logs
Remediation: Mask or truncate logs; audit access

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: Replay Attack via SMTP Queue Tampering
output:
Attacker tampers with the mail queue directory on a Linux-based SMTP server to reintroduce previously sent messages.
Vulnerability: Queue file access, root compromise
Impact: False re-delivery, spam, insider fraud
Detection: Monitor queue activity, alert on resends
Remediation: Restrict queue file permissions

instruction: Describe the Message Replay attack: Message Replay via SMTP-to-SMTP Tunneling
output:
Attacker uses SMTP tunnels between compromised servers to replay messages across internal and external boundaries.
Vulnerability: Tunneling misuse, SMTP proxy chaining
Impact: External leak of internal mail
Detection: Inspect unusual SMTP traffic ports
Remediation: Disallow outbound SMTP tunnels

instruction: Describe the Abusing Email Auto-forwarding Rules attack: Hidden Auto-Forward Rule to Attacker Email
output:
Attacker gains access to a user's mailbox and silently adds an auto-forward rule to send a copy of every received email to their own email address.
Vulnerability: Insecure mailbox rules not monitored
Impact: Sensitive data leaks, intellectual property theft
Detection: Monitor rules via PowerShell or security tools for external forwarding
Remediation: Disable external auto-forwarding and alert on rule creation

instruction: Describe the Abusing Email Auto-forwarding Rules attack: Auto-Forward Triggered by Specific Keywords
output:
Auto-forwarding rule filters emails based on sensitive terms like “invoice”, “bank”, “password” and sends only those to attacker’s inbox.
Vulnerability: Misused client-side rules for keyword-triggered forwarding
Impact: Confidential financial info leaked to attacker
Detection: Log and audit Outlook rules regularly
Remediation: Block user-level forwarding via group policy

instruction: Describe the Abusing Email Auto-forwarding Rules attack: Rule Injection via Compromised Admin Account
output:
Attacker compromises Exchange Admin account and injects auto-forward rules into multiple mailboxes.
Vulnerability: Admin-level privilege abuse, rule injection
Impact: Enterprise-wide data leakage
Detection: Audit Exchange rules and monitor command logs
