Vulnerability: Model replacement via static file injection
Impact: Unauthorized access, bypassed checks
Detection: Monitor app behavior or validate model hashes during runtime
Remediation: Code-sign models; verify ONNX file integrity at app startup

instruction: Describe the Backdoor attack: Trojaned AI Model in Mobile App
output:
A model embedded in a mobile app performs normally but is secretly trained to behave maliciously when triggered by a specific pattern.
Vulnerability: Triggered backdoor in AI model logic
Impact: Conditional privilege escalation, access leak
Detection: Runtime monitoring, anomaly-based input testing
Remediation: Use trusted, signed models only; audit training pipeline; test with adversarial triggers

instruction: Describe the Visual Exploit attack: Image Perturbation Against AR or Vision App
output:
Subtle image manipulation causes AR apps or vision-based mobile apps to misbehave, crash, or show unintended behavior.
Vulnerability: Adversarial image input bypassing ML logic
Impact: DoS, visual misclassification, trust breakdown
Detection: Log unusual misclassification patterns; validate input format and characteristics
Remediation: Train models with adversarial robustness; apply visual integrity checks before inference

instruction: Describe the Input Spoofing attack: Fake Sensor Data for Activity Recognition ML
output:
Attacker crafts or injects fake motion, GPS, or sensor data to fool ML models used in fitness or location-based mobile apps.
Vulnerability: Trusting local sensors without validation
Impact: Bypass of health tracking, insurance fraud
Detection: Compare GPS + accelerometer data for realism; root detection; detect repeated/suspicious patterns
Remediation: Use server-side validation of sensor patterns; block rooted/jailbroken devices

instruction: Describe the Stealing attack: Model Extraction via Query Attack
output:
Repeatedly querying the ML model in a mobile app to reconstruct it offline, gaining insight into logic or IP.
Vulnerability: Exposure of model logic to uncontrolled queries
Impact: IP theft, evasion crafting, black-box misuse
Detection: Log and monitor repeated query patterns; alert on too-fast or similar input burst
Remediation: Use rate limiting, watermarking of ML outputs, secure model distribution

instruction: Describe the Privacy Attack attack: Membership Inference on Mobile Models
output:
Attacker tries to determine whether a specific user’s data was part of the ML training set by probing model confidence outputs.
Vulnerability: Overconfident model output on training data
Impact: Privacy violation, dataset inference
Detection: Compare model behavior across input set; use auditing tools like ML Privacy Meter
Remediation: Use DP training, output rounding, model dropout layers

instruction: Describe the Real-Time Attack attack: Gradient-Based Perturbation Crafting on Mobile Camera Feed
output:
Real-time perturbation of live mobile camera feed using gradient-based adversarial methods to mislead object detection models like YOLO, SSD, or MobileNet.
Vulnerability: Vision model sensitivity to crafted input
Impact: Real-time ML misdirection, surveillance evasion
Detection: Monitor frame-by-frame anomaly; measure pixel noise entropy
Remediation: Use adversarial training; input smoothing and noise filters

instruction: Describe the Offline Evasion attack: White-box Attack on Exported Mobile Models
output:
Attackers analyze exported .tflite or .mlmodel files from mobile apps to reverse-engineer and craft adversarial inputs targeting specific model weaknesses.
Vulnerability: Plaintext models allow analysis and tuning
Impact: Precision evasion, authentication bypass
Detection: Monitor model access and extraction patterns from app builds
Remediation: Encrypt model weights; use server-side inference; adversarial defense layers

instruction: Describe the Runtime Tamper attack: Model Inference Hijack via Frida
output:
Use Frida to hook into Android ML inference libraries and intercept or alter classification results at runtime.
Vulnerability: Unprotected ML inference pipeline at runtime
Impact: Prediction spoofing, fraud, bypass
Detection: Detect Frida instrumentation, attach anti-debugger methods
Remediation: Use native code integrity verification; check call stack consistency

instruction: Describe the Visual Backdoor attack: On-Device Adversarial Patch Attack
output:
Physical or digital adversarial patch added to input images (e.g., sticker on object) fools the vision model in mobile apps.
Vulnerability: Visual model’s fragility to spatial noise
Impact: Evasion of object recognition, face spoofing
Detection: Train patch detection models; monitor for specific pixel patterns in captured input
Remediation: Use adversarial training with patch noise; enable multi-frame validation to confirm object identity

instruction: Describe the Phonetic Attack attack: Voice Assistant Wakeword Bypass
output:
Use an adversarial audio input that sounds different to humans but is interpreted as the wake word by the AI voice assistant (e.g., “Ok Google” or “Hey Siri”).
Vulnerability: Wake word phoneme similarity trick
Impact: Unauthorized device access via voice trigger
Detection: Monitor unexpected audio pattern activations; detect acoustic anomalies
Remediation: Use speaker recognition or liveness detection for wake words

instruction: Describe the Spoofing attack: Fake Biometric Inputs via Adversarial Image
output:
Use adversarially crafted face/fingerprint images to fool AI-based biometric systems in mobile apps or unlock mechanisms.
Vulnerability: Model fooled by adversarial input
Impact: Account takeover, biometric bypass
Detection: Use entropy-based or patch-based biometric verification; detect repeated matching failures
Remediation: Combine biometric with liveness detection (e.g., blink, movement); use adversarially hardened models

instruction: Describe the Supply Chain attack: Trojan Injection via Ad Network SDK
output:
An attacker includes a backdoored AI model or malicious logic inside a popular advertising SDK used in mobile apps.
Vulnerability: Hidden logic in third-party mobile dependencies
Impact: Mass device compromise, secret exfiltration
Detection: Monitor SDK behavior at runtime; scan APKs for suspicious URLs or logic
Remediation: Use verified SDKs only; perform behavioral sandboxing on all dependencies

instruction: Describe the Poisoning attack: Model Drift Attack in Mobile Learning Systems
output:
Many mobile apps use on-device learning (e.g., keyboard suggestions, fitness apps). Adversaries poison user data that the model learns from over time.
Vulnerability: Unvalidated fine-tuning on poisoned user data
Impact: Long-term model degradation or misuse
Detection: Monitor data sources and patterns used for local model training; set model boundaries
Remediation: Harden on-device learning using secure enclaves; filter and validate input before feeding into local ML

instruction: Describe the External Signal attack: Adversarial ML Attack via Bluetooth Device Input
output:
Adversary uses wearable devices (e.g., smartwatches, keyboards, IoT toys) to inject adversarial signals into mobile ML models like gesture, audio, or text input.
Vulnerability: Implicit trust in external peripheral inputs
Impact: Misclassification, remote manipulation of models
Detection: Monitor and whitelist trusted BLE MAC addresses; check for abnormal frequency in data streams
Remediation: Require strong pairing verification; include origin metadata with sensor data

instruction: Describe the UI Injection attack: In-app LLM Prompt Manipulation via UI Inputs
output:
Apps embedding local/remote LLMs often use UI fields to generate prompts. A malicious user can manipulate input fields to trigger harmful or escalated responses.
Vulnerability: Improper prompt isolation from user input
Impact: Data leakage, LLM misuse or escalation
Detection: Log prompt inputs vs generated completions; apply strict output format validation
Remediation: Implement prompt escaping/sandboxing; isolate user input from template control phrases

instruction: Describe the Supply Chain attack: Compromised ML Model in Mobile Update
output:
Mobile apps often auto-download updated AI/ML models (e.g., for recommendations, image classification). If the update source is compromised, a poisoned model may be deployed silently.
Vulnerability: Insecure update of model files over network
Impact: Remote model manipulation and logic compromise
Detection: Monitor app’s outbound connections and hash downloaded files; check for unexpected behavior shifts
Remediation: Sign and verify downloaded models; use secure HTTPS and integrity checks (SHA256, digital sigs)

instruction: Describe the Binary Swap attack: Dynamic Model Replacement via Storage Injection
output:
On rooted devices, attackers can overwrite the stored model file with a poisoned or Trojanized one to hijack app behavior.
Vulnerability: Lack of model file validation at runtime
Impact: Local RCE, ML evasion, logic manipulation
Detection: Check hash of model files on app launch; log unexpected storage writes
Remediation: Secure model files with permission hardening; verify model hash on load; detect tampering via checksum

instruction: Describe the Adversarial Evasion attack: Black-box Adversarial Image Creation via On-device Inference
output:
Attacker uses on-device inference (e.g., object detection or face unlock) to iteratively craft adversarial images that cause the model to misbehave.
Vulnerability: Lack of adversarial defense in inference logic
Impact: Model bypass, false classification
Detection: Use adversarial detection filters; track unusual inference patterns
Remediation: Add adversarial training; use input sanitization and confidence-based rejection

instruction: Describe the Poisoning attack: Label Flipping in On-device Active Learning
output:
Some mobile apps re-train their AI models using feedback or labels provided by users. If a malicious user submits incorrect labels, the model learns wrong behavior.
Vulnerability: Trust on user-labeled input without validation
Impact: ML corruption, spam evasion, unsafe recommendations
Detection: Monitor labeling trends; flag inconsistent or bulk label changes
Remediation: Validate label inputs with consensus or human moderation; train using verified/clean datasets

instruction: Describe the Input Spoofing attack: Adversarial QR Codes in Mobile Scanner Apps
output:
QR scanner apps with ML-powered OCR or smart action parsing can be tricked using visually manipulated QR codes to perform unintended actions.
Vulnerability: Weak parsing/OCR logic for QR actions
Impact: Phishing, remote control, link hijack
Detection: Analyze QR parsing logic; use checksum or context validation
Remediation: Validate parsed actions before triggering; add user confirmation step

instruction: Describe the ML Evasion attack: Visual CAPTCHA Bypass via Perturbation
output:
Mobile apps using AI-powered CAPTCHA (image or text-based puzzles) can be tricked with slightly modified inputs that humans can’t notice but ML misinterprets.
Vulnerability: ML misclassification on perturbed visual input
Impact: CAPTCHA bypass, bot entry, auth evasion
Detection: Monitor unusual success rates; detect repeated visual pattern attempts
Remediation: Use multi-factor CAPTCHA including user interaction checks (clicks, speed, randomness); improve model robustness

instruction: Describe the Model Weakening attack: DNN Quantization Abuse
output:
Attackers exploit the precision loss from quantization (e.g., in .tflite files) to mislead the model and force misclassification on mobile devices.
Vulnerability: Low-precision ops in quantized models
Impact: Bypass object detection, content moderation
Detection: Monitor for consistent borderline classification; compare results from quantized and full-precision models
Remediation: Use robust quantization-aware training; apply input sanitization before model inference

instruction: Describe the Sensor Attack attack: Noise Injection into Mobile Mic for Adversarial Audio
output:
Attackers emit ultrasonic or high-frequency sounds that can't be heard by humans but are picked up by phone microphones and misinterpreted by ML models.
Vulnerability: ML over-trust in audio without origin validation
Impact: Unauthorized command execution, data leakage
Detection: Monitor for high-frequency audio during idle; log unexpected voice input triggers
Remediation: Filter out frequencies above 16kHz; apply microphone signal preprocessing (anti-ultrasonic) before ML processing

instruction: Describe the Deployment Attack attack: APK Tampering to Modify Model Parameters
output:
Attackers reverse-engineer a mobile APK, locate bundled AI model files, and manually modify weight or bias parameters to degrade or alter ML behavior.
Vulnerability: Lack of model integrity check in APK files
Impact: Faulty predictions, RCE, privacy bypass
Detection: Validate model file hash; monitor runtime model behavior against expected output
Remediation: Use signed models; enforce hash checks at runtime; encrypt models in APK

instruction: Describe the Branding Abuse attack: Adversarial Logo Attack on Object Detectors
output:
Attackers slightly modify brand logos (e.g., rotate, color shift, pixel tweak) so that object detection models on mobile AR/camera apps either fail or misidentify them.
Vulnerability: Over-reliance on vision models for detection
Impact: Brand spoofing, misreporting, AR filter abuse
Detection: Image logging, confidence thresholds in object detection
Remediation: Apply adversarial training to models; use multi-modal verification (e.g., logo + text + barcode); restrict user-generated logos

instruction: Describe the Visual AR Exploit attack: Physical-World Mobile AR Misdirection
output:
By physically manipulating surroundings or camera view, attackers can mislead mobile AR apps into misplacing or misinterpreting virtual content.
Vulnerability: Image/marker tracking without strong validation
Impact: Confusion, misdirection, manipulation of AR views
Detection: Use AR debug logging; analyze object placement vs expected coordinates
Remediation: Use encrypted or verified tracking images; limit AR responses to trusted anchors only

instruction: Describe the Input Evasion attack: Transferable Adversarial Image Attack
output:
Adversarial images crafted for one AI model like MobileNet can still fool other models like ResNet or YOLO, even if the attacker never touched them directly.
Vulnerability: Lack of robustness across models
Impact: Multi-app AI evasion, model-agnostic spoofing
Detection: Visual logging, detection mismatch, model disagreement
Remediation: Train models with adversarial samples; add image filters to detect pixel-level adversarial noise

instruction: Describe the Prompt Poisoning attack: Cross-LLM Prompt Injection Transfer
output:
Prompt injections crafted for one LLM (like GPT) can often fool others (like Claude, Gemini, etc.) because they use similar parsing and memory styles.
Vulnerability: Shared parsing logic in LLMs
Impact: LLM misuse across apps, phishing, policy bypass
Detection: Look for patterns of prompt injection, repeated command misfires
Remediation: Apply input validation, sandbox prompt context, use injection-safe templates

instruction: Describe the Context Injection Hijack attack: Multi-Agent Behavior Hijack via Shared Context
output:
If multiple AI agents share memory (e.g., LangChain or Android AI modules), a malicious agent can silently alter the shared context, affecting behavior of all agents.
Vulnerability: Shared memory context between agents
Impact: Cross-agent takeover, policy manipulation
Detection: Analyze shared prompt memory, look for policy-conflicting outputs
Remediation: Isolate agent memory, restrict shared context, purge memory on switch

instruction: Describe the Query Transfer Attack attack: Black-Box Transfer Adversarial Attack
output:
Even without knowing how the target ML model works internally, attackers build adversarial inputs using a surrogate model. These often work on the real model too.
Vulnerability: Model generalization weaknesses
Impact: Model evasion without internal access
Detection: Look for similar misclassifications across multiple inputs and platforms
Remediation: Use adversarial training, ensemble models, or add randomized input smoothing filters

instruction: Describe the Portability Exploit attack: Cross-Architecture Model Exploitation
output:
Adversarial samples generated for TFLite-based models also work on ONNX, CoreML, or PyTorch models despite architectural differences.
Vulnerability: Inconsistent preprocessing between formats
Impact: Multi-platform AI evasion
Detection: Discrepancy in predictions across model backends or formats
Remediation: Normalize input pipelines across models; use adversarial input detectors

instruction: Describe the Universal Input Spoofing attack: Universal Adversarial Perturbation (UAP)
output:
UAPs are small invisible changes that can be added to any image, causing misclassification regardless of the image's content.
Vulnerability: Lack of universal perturbation resistance
Impact: Cross-input, scalable misclassification
Detection: Watch for consistent wrong outputs across large image batches
Remediation: Use model ensembles, train with adversarial UAP examples, or detect perturbation patterns

instruction: Describe the Optimization-Based Evasion attack: Gradient Sign Transfer Across Models
output:
Adversarial examples created using just the sign of the gradient in one model (e.g., TFLite) can often transfer and fool similar models with different architectures.
Vulnerability: Gradient sign similarities across models
Impact: Cross-model adversarial image misclassification
Detection: Monitor for perturbed image similarity across inputs; monitor model error patterns
Remediation: Train models with adversarial examples and use randomized smoothing techniques

instruction: Describe the Poisoned Pretraining attack: Malicious Training Data Transfer
output:
A poisoned dataset is used during pretraining on one system (e.g., by an open-source contributor), and its effects carry into downstream models, even on other platforms.
Vulnerability: Data supply chain (poisoned dataset reuse)
Impact: Persistent hidden backdoor in production ML apps
Detection: Audit datasets for labeling anomalies, outliers; analyze predictions against rare triggers
Remediation: Curate datasets; perform anomaly detection during training; use certified clean datasets

instruction: Describe the Cross-Platform ML Backdoor attack: Platform-Agnostic Trojan Model Activation
output:
A trojaned model is inserted into an app on Android using TFLite, and the same poisoned model works across platforms like iOS (CoreML), Windows (ONNX), or even browsers (WebML).
Vulnerability: Hidden backdoor logic in model weights
Impact: Cross-device persistent trigger activation
Detection: Monitor unusual input patterns causing consistent misbehavior; audit all pretrained models before conversion
Remediation: Train clean models; verify model behavior with unseen inputs; use model fingerprinting tools like Netron

instruction: Describe the LLM Bias Triggering attack: Prompt Engineering for Bias Retrieval
output:
Attackers craft very specific prompts that are designed to bypass content filters and retrieve biased, hateful, or discriminatory content hidden within the LLM’s latent space.
Vulnerability: Prompt bypass of bias protection
Impact: Toxic content leakage, reputational harm
Detection: Analyze prompt patterns; flag loaded/questionable phrasing
Remediation: Train models with counter-biasing; use automated content moderation pipelines

instruction: Describe the Cross-modal Bias attack: Bias Transfer in Multimodal Models
output:
Bias is introduced in one modality (e.g., text) and gets transferred into the other (e.g., vision), causing unfair responses from multimodal models like CLIP or Gemini.
Vulnerability: Paired modality bias transfer
Impact: Cross-modal racism, unfair AI perception
Detection: Visualize embedding similarity; compare per-group output for same prompt
Remediation: Clean captions; apply cross-modal debiasing during training; evaluate with synthetic fair prompts

instruction: Describe the Reinforcement Learning Bias attack: Unfair Reward Shaping in RL
output:
Attackers shape the reward function during RL training to favor certain actions or demographics, teaching the agent to behave in discriminatory or skewed ways.
Vulnerability: Reward logic abuse
Impact: Reinforced bias in decision-making AI
Detection: Compare policy decisions across demographics; inspect reward logs
Remediation: Enforce fairness constraints in reward design; simulate diverse users in training

instruction: Describe the Preprocessing Exploit attack: Biased Filtering Pipelines
output:
Attackers manipulate data filters during preprocessing to exclude images, texts, or samples from certain groups (e.g., darker skin tones, non-English languages) — reducing representation and accuracy.
Vulnerability: Filtering threshold unfair to minorities
Impact: Underperformance or exclusion of specific groups
Detection: Visual audit of filtered vs retained dataset; pixel-intensity bias analysis
Remediation: Use fairness-aware filters; track demographic retention rate in preprocessing

instruction: Describe the Metric Exploitation attack: Evaluation Metric Gaming
output:
Developers (intentionally or not) select biased evaluation metrics like overall accuracy, ignoring fairness scores — making unfair models look good during validation and deployment.
Vulnerability: Misleading metric choice
Impact: Unfair deployment of biased systems
Detection: Measure fairness metrics: demographic parity, TPR gaps, equalized odds
Remediation: Always report group-wise metrics; avoid using only overall accuracy as decision criterion

instruction: Describe the Online Drift attack: Bias Reinforcement via Online Learning
output:
In systems that continuously learn from user feedback, toxic or biased feedback loops (e.g., racist reports or flags) get learned by the model, reinforcing discrimination.
Vulnerability: Feedback loop poisoning
Impact: Persistent model discrimination against groups
Detection: Monitor feedback origin; track changing model behavior across time and user types
Remediation: Use feedback delay buffers, validate feedback fairness, avoid real-time weight updates without audit

instruction: Describe the Prompt Jailbreak attack: Bias-Aware Jailbreak Prompts
output:
Attackers craft prompts that acknowledge bias filters but use logic traps or hypothetical framing to trick the model into outputting restricted or discriminatory content.
Vulnerability: Prompt filter bypass using bias framing
Impact: Bypass of safety filters; toxic output generation
Detection: Analyze prompt context; use prompt classifier for intent rather than text only
Remediation: Integrate deeper safety classifiers, teach models to refuse role-play that leads to bias speech

instruction: Describe the Fairness Robustness Attack attack: Adversarial Group Attacks
output:
Craft adversarial inputs (images, text) that cause misclassification only for a specific group, without affecting others — exposing lack of group-level robustness.
Vulnerability: Demographic-sensitive robustness gap
Impact: Group-specific discrimination, bias under attacks
Detection: Test adversarial robustness separately per demographic; track which groups fail under perturbations
Remediation: Train with group-agnostic adversarial examples; use fairness-aware robustness loss functions

instruction: Describe the Recommendation Bias attack: Discriminatory Ranking Attack
output:
Attackers game recommendation systems by flooding the platform with positive interactions for favored group items, causing the system to downrank other groups.
Vulnerability: Feedback loop manipulation
Impact: Systemic visibility suppression of certain groups
Detection: Monitor for ranking shifts across demographics; detect suspicious interaction bursts
Remediation: Use diversity-aware ranking logic; penalize bot-like behavior; normalize per-group exposure

instruction: Describe the Model Poisoning via Feedback attack: Toxic Fine-tuning Campaign
output:
Attackers mass-upload biased or toxic content to platforms where models learn from user-generated data (e.g., Reddit, review sites), poisoning the model’s future behavior.
Vulnerability: Biased RLHF data pollution
Impact: Loss of model neutrality, toxic alignment
Detection: Compare pre- and post-tuning responses on fairness prompts; audit training source logs
Remediation: Filter crowd-sourced input; train on curated datasets only; use differential feedback validation

instruction: Describe the Training Data Exploitation attack: Crowdsourced Bias Injection
output:
Large datasets gathered via crowdsourcing (e.g., Mechanical Turk, labeling platforms) can be biased if workers hold stereotypes or make labeling errors that favor one group.
Vulnerability: Annotation bias from crowdworkers
Impact: Long-term bias in trained models
Detection: Compare label agreement across demographics; test model with counterfactual examples
Remediation: Write clear labeling instructions; balance annotator backgrounds; filter biased labels using audits

instruction: Describe the Underrepresentation attack: Feature Suppression Attack
output:
Certain useful features are intentionally excluded or zeroed out for one demographic group (e.g., education level for women), reducing model accuracy or score unfairly.
Vulnerability: Group-specific feature removal
Impact: Unfair predictions, suppressed group accuracy
Detection: Analyze per-group feature presence matrix; test with counterfactual imputation
Remediation: Ensure uniform feature treatment across groups; enforce schema equality during preprocessing

instruction: Describe the Fairness Test Failure Exploit attack: Counterfactual Disparity Attack
output:
By submitting identical inputs except for one sensitive field (e.g., gender), attackers show the model gives different results — proving bias through controlled input swaps.
Vulnerability: Counterfactual inconsistency
Impact: Legal and ethical failure in AI predictions
Detection: Run A/B input tests; track differences in outputs for minimal input deltas
Remediation: Enforce counterfactual fairness during training and testing; regular auditing across sensitive fields

instruction: Describe the Societal Exploit attack: Unfair Resource Allocation via ML
output:
ML models used for real-world decisions (loans, housing, jobs) reflect and amplify bias — allocating fewer resources to minorities by predicting them as higher risk unfairly.
Vulnerability: Legacy bias learning from historical data
Impact: Long-term systemic inequality enforcement
Detection: Track group-wise output disparities; use AI model explainers (e.g., SHAP, LIME)
Remediation: De-bias training data; apply fairness constraints; block sensitive attributes from model access

instruction: Describe the Geographic Discrimination attack: In-the-wild Redlining via AI
output:
Models are trained to indirectly block services (e.g., insurance, lending, ads) in areas populated by minorities or low-income communities using ZIP codes or geolocation.
Vulnerability: Proxy discrimination using geography
Impact: Discriminatory service access by location
Detection: Analyze predictions across regions; compare ZIP-level patterns
Remediation: Remove ZIP code unless necessary; cluster locations by need, not wealth/race; fairness tuning on location groups

instruction: Describe the Dataset Quality Manipulation attack: Bias via Missing Data Exploit
output:
Some groups have more missing or corrupted data (e.g., minorities in medical datasets), leading to poor performance on them — attackers exploit this to reduce model fairness.
Vulnerability: Missingness-related group bias
Impact: Inaccurate predictions for already underrepresented groups
Detection: Visualize missing value ratios by group; test model performance per group
Remediation: Use group-aware imputation; flag and balance missing values; avoid discriminatory fill logic

instruction: Describe the Audit/Explainability Evasion attack: Attribution Misdirection
output:
Attackers manipulate ML pipelines or outputs to mislead auditing tools, researchers, or explainability systems about the true source or cause of model behavior.
Vulnerability: Model explanation layer manipulation
Impact: False assurance of fairness, audit deception
Detection: Use counterfactual testing, feature leakage analysis, attention visualization tools
Remediation: Validate attribution tools with external fairness probes; cross-check explanations with multiple methods

instruction: Describe the Code Injection via Interpretation attack: Explainability API Injection
output:
Malicious users inject payloads into inputs that are parsed by SHAP/LIME or model explainability tools, exploiting how these tools use Python eval() or unsafe parsing routines.
Vulnerability: Unsafe eval/exec usage in explanation interfaces
Impact: Remote code execution, data theft during explanation
Detection: Scan for eval or exec in code paths; test inputs with payloads; use secure logging
Remediation: Avoid dynamic code execution in interpretability code; use strict input sanitation and sandboxed SHAP execution

instruction: Describe the Hidden Data Leak via Attribution attack: Steganographic Feature Encoding
output:
Attackers embed binary data into SHAP or attention explanations, using explanation outputs as covert channels to exfiltrate training data.
Vulnerability: Covert channel via attribution encoding
Impact: Secret leakage of training data or private model state
Detection: Entropy analysis of SHAP values; track repeated high/low attributions across samples
Remediation: Add noise/randomization to attribution outputs; verify attribution patterns don’t leak consistent data

instruction: Describe the Poisoned Input Explanation Trick attack: Input Poisoning to Fool SHAP
output:
Attacker injects samples into training data that distort model explanations — making SHAP highlight irrelevant features or masking the true driver features of predictions.
Vulnerability: Feature importance manipulation via poisoning
Impact: False trust in explanations; misinformed audits
Detection: Analyze SHAP output shifts across clean and noisy training splits; test attribution variance
Remediation: Clean and robust training data; run attribution diagnostics during model audits

instruction: Describe the Model Inversion via Explanation attack: Model Inversion via SHAP Probing
output:
Attackers query SHAP with controlled inputs and infer sensitive training data by reverse-engineering model gradients and important feature patterns.
Vulnerability: SHAP-based leakage of training data patterns
Impact: Training data disclosure, privacy breach
Detection: Detect unusual querying of attribution tools; rate-limit and log attribution requests
Remediation: Limit attribution output access; add explanation noise; aggregate attribution rather than expose individual details

instruction: Describe the Misleading Reasoning via Explainability attack: Counterfactual Manipulation
output:
Attackers manipulate how counterfactuals are generated (e.g., “what-if” examples) to make harmful or unfair decisions appear fair by producing unrealistic or cherry-picked changes.
Vulnerability: Counterfactual generation tampering
Impact: Regulatory evasion, user deception, audit blindness
Detection: Audit counterfactual diversity; test predictions across full feature space
Remediation: Enforce transparent counterfactual logic; test with adversarial fairness frameworks

instruction: Describe the Caching Exploit via Explanation API attack: Explainability Replay Attack
output:
Attackers abuse cached explanation data (e.g., SHAP values or attention maps) to impersonate other users or forge valid-looking explanations for queries they never made.
Vulnerability: Cache key misuse in explainability engines
Impact: User impersonation, data leakage, audit forgery
Detection: Monitor cache access per user; detect cache key collisions or reuse across users
Remediation: Isolate caches by user/session; add auth headers and nonces to cache identifiers

instruction: Describe the Attribution Bias Detection attack: Cross-Example Attribution Abuse
output:
Attackers analyze and compare SHAP or LIME outputs for very similar inputs to detect biased patterns in the model, e.g., race or gender being unfairly weighted.
Vulnerability: Attribution reveals hidden model bias
Impact: Discovery of model’s unfair logic through explanation
Detection: Use counterfactual tests; track attribution drift between sensitive identity values
Remediation: Reduce feature dependency on identity variables; audit SHAP attribution using fairness toolkits

instruction: Describe the Feature Attribution Poisoning attack: Adversarial Feature Importance Tuning
output:
Attackers manipulate the model training phase so SHAP/LIME explanations show misleading or decoy features as important, concealing true decision logic or biases.
Vulnerability: SHAP output misdirection via data poisoning
Impact: Misinformed audits, hidden model bias
Detection: Monitor attribution consistency across training sessions; test against known clean and poisoned data samples
Remediation: Train with robust datasets; use attribution anomaly detection; verify explanations against clean benchmarks

instruction: Describe the Overload Exploit via Input Bloat attack: Explanation Flooding Attack
output:
Attacker generates extremely long or complex input (e.g., huge text or image with dense features) that breaks or slows down explanation tools like SHAP/LIME.
Vulnerability: Resource exhaustion via long inputs
Impact: DoS, broken explanations, UI crash
Detection: Monitor explanation run time; log long token input cases; add timeout protections
Remediation: Limit input size; pre-process text for explainability; use fallback attribution modes

instruction: Describe the Output Sabotage attack: Targeted Explanation Discrediting
output:
Attacker poisons the model or explanations so that specific users always see confusing, false, or nonsensical attributions — undermining trust in the system.
Vulnerability: Personalized explanation sabotage
Impact: Trust loss, targeted sabotage of audits
Detection: Compare SHAP results across users for same inputs; scan for attribution drift by user ID
Remediation: Use identity-agnostic attribution; remove conditional explanation branches in code

instruction: Describe the NLP Bias Attack attack: Adversarial Token Selection
output:
Attackers select tokens that SHAP or LIME incorrectly assign high importance to, even though they are semantically meaningless. Exploits tokenization artifacts or subword splits.
Vulnerability: SHAP/LIME misattribution on token artifacts
Impact: Misleading explanations, hidden bias
Detection: Track token frequency vs attribution importance; highlight high SHAP scores on garbage tokens
Remediation: Normalize attributions across subtokens; penalize high attribution on rare/meaningless tokens

instruction: Describe the Fairness Evasion attack: Bias Masking via Explanation Drift
output:
Model is trained in a way that it distributes SHAP/LIME values uniformly across all features, hiding real bias by masking importance differences.
Vulnerability: Deliberate masking of attribution patterns
Impact: Undetectable bias, failed fairness audits
Detection: Analyze SHAP attribution variance; test across diverse demographic groups
Remediation: Use multiple bias audits; avoid relying solely on SHAP/LIME for fairness validation

instruction: Describe the Information Leakage attack: Explainability API as Oracle
output:
SHAP or LIME is misused as a black-box oracle by attackers to extract internal model behavior and logic, even without knowing model weights or architecture.
Vulnerability: Attribution as oracle for model internals
Impact: Feature extraction, reverse-engineered model logic
Detection: Rate-limit explanation endpoints; detect high-volume attribute probing
Remediation: Obfuscate SHAP APIs; apply differential privacy; disable full explanations for public users

instruction: Describe the Backdoor Attribution Manipulation attack: Backdoor Activation Attribution Confusion
output:
Model is trained with a backdoor trigger (e.g., special word or pixel pattern) but SHAP/LIME shows confusing or misleading attribution when the backdoor is activated.
Vulnerability: SHAP attribution hides true backdoor feature
Impact: Hidden backdoors undetectable via explanation tools
Detection: Compare SHAP between clean and triggered inputs; look for trigger-feature attribution mismatch
Remediation: Perform attribution-aware auditing; use backdoor-detection with explanation heatmap analysis

instruction: Describe the Exploit Refinement attack: Explainability-Guided Prompt Engineering
output:
Attackers use LLM explainability tools (like token-level SHAP or attention maps) to guide crafting of malicious prompts that bypass filters or change outputs subtly.
Vulnerability: Overreliance on token importance exposure
Impact: Jailbreak success, filter evasion, offensive outputs
Detection: Detect repeated, attribution-driven refinements; analyze prompt logs for semantic-adversarial shifts
Remediation: Obfuscate token attribution APIs; restrict logprobs/SHAP for public-facing LLMs

instruction: Describe the Model Stealing attack: Model Extraction via Explainability Calls
output:
Attackers use repeated SHAP/LIME probing to reverse-engineer the model’s decision boundary or logic and reconstruct a surrogate model.
Vulnerability: SHAP/LIME revealing model logic over time
Impact: Intellectual property theft, clone model generation
Detection: Monitor excessive SHAP/LIME usage patterns; limit explanation queries per API key
Remediation: Use differential privacy in explanations; rate-limit access to SHAP APIs

instruction: Describe the Prompt Injection Aid attack: Explainability for Prompt Injection Debugging
output:
LLM jailbreakers use explainability tools to identify which parts of their input trigger safety filters, helping refine and succeed in prompt injections.
Vulnerability: Exposed filter logic via explanation
Impact: Filter bypass, offensive or policy-violating prompts
Detection: Monitor sequences of modified prompts; detect prompt engineering loops
Remediation: Obfuscate SHAP/logprobs; implement prompt perturbation noise

instruction: Describe the Explainability-Induced Fairness Failure attack: Attention Heatmap Bias Amplification
output:
Models trained to highlight attention on neutral tokens while hiding true biased reasoning in other attention heads or layers.
Vulnerability: Misleading explanations from shallow attention
Impact: Biased behavior hidden under fair-looking explanations
Detection: Audit attention across layers; test attributions on counterfactual demographic inputs
Remediation: Require explainability at multiple layers; avoid attention-only fairness claims

instruction: Describe the User Re-identification attack: Explanation Fingerprinting Attack
output:
SHAP or LIME explanation outputs are used to uniquely "fingerprint" users or specific inputs, potentially revealing identity or usage patterns.
Vulnerability: Predictable, unique attribution patterns
Impact: Privacy violation, user de-anonymization
Detection: Monitor repeated explanation pattern comparisons across sessions; track metadata of SHAP/LIME output use
Remediation: Add noise to SHAP/LIME outputs; limit resolution or detail exposed; rate-limit or restrict external access

instruction: Describe the Output Exploit attack: Explainability-Guided Prompt Injection (LLMs)
output:
LLM attackers use SHAP/attention scores to identify and remove the "safe" tokens responsible for refusals, enabling prompt injection and jailbreaks.
Vulnerability: Token-level explainability reveals filters
Impact: Filter evasion, malicious content generation
Detection: Track prompt evolution patterns; monitor high similarity inputs that converge toward harmful output
Remediation: Limit logprobs/SHAP for unsafe outputs; obfuscate internal token attributions; train LLMs to defend against input variations

instruction: Describe the Reasoning Exploit attack: LLM Misleading Chain-of-Thought Attribution
output:
LLMs may generate chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning that appears logical, but actual SHAP or attention maps show the real decision was made elsewhere or earlier.
Vulnerability: Fabricated reasoning via CoT mismatch
Impact: False trust in LLM reasoning, hallucination abuse
Detection: Check if SHAP values match CoT logic; use logic verifiers to confirm consistency of generated reasoning
Remediation: Align CoT generation with attribution; penalize hallucinated logic paths

instruction: Describe the Fairness Analysis Abuse attack: Explainability API Misuse for Bias Probing
output:
Attackers use explanation APIs (like SHAP) to probe how differently the model treats different demographics, leaking bias or sensitive internal rules.
Vulnerability: Explanation APIs exposing demographic behavior
Impact: Public exposure of unfair model decisions
Detection: Detect systematic demographic toggling in API calls; rate-limit fairness audit behavior
Remediation: Limit access to SHAP on sensitive fields; inject randomness or use cohort-based explanations

instruction: Describe the Adversarial Subversion attack: Hidden Trigger Attribution Manipulation
output:
During training, the attacker ensures that hidden backdoor trigger tokens contribute zero or very low SHAP attribution, making them invisible to audits.
Vulnerability: Attribution-evading model backdoors
Impact: Undetectable model backdoors, bypassed audits
Detection: Compare outputs and SHAP values across clean and poisoned samples; test importance of zero-attribution tokens
Remediation: Randomize training; monitor attribution consistency across inputs; penalize under-attributed but impactful tokens

instruction: Describe the Explainability Misuse / False Trust attack: Overconfidence in Explainability Outputs
output:
Attackers or even developers place excessive trust in SHAP/LIME outputs without validating them, assuming they reflect true model reasoning — even when they don’t.
Vulnerability: Misleading attribution creating false confidence
Impact: Hidden bias or logic masked as fair, audit evasion
Detection: Detect inconsistency between model predictions and explanation deltas across similar samples
Remediation: Use multiple XAI tools (SHAP, LIME, Integrated Gradients); validate outputs using controlled and adversarial test inputs

instruction: Describe the Static Analysis attack: Model File Extraction from App
output:
Attackers extract deployed ML models (like .onnx, .tflite, .mlmodel) from Android/iOS apps or edge devices to reverse-engineer or steal logic.
Vulnerability: Lack of model obfuscation or encryption
Impact: Intellectual property theft, attack prep (e.g., adversarial inputs)
Detection: Monitor for app reverse engineering patterns; check for modified APKs in wild
Remediation: Encrypt models before embedding, use runtime decryption, add anti-tamper checks, or use model watermarking

instruction: Describe the Graph Inspection / Reverse Engineering attack: ONNX Graph Parsing Attack
output:
Attackers analyze the computation graph of a stolen or extracted ONNX model to understand how the model works, extract logic, and prepare for cloning or exploitation.
Vulnerability: Unprotected model file with parseable graph
Impact: Full model cloning, IP theft, adversarial prep
Detection: Monitor for suspicious access to ONNX files; track model access logs
Remediation: Use model obfuscation, encrypted ONNX storage, graph anonymization, or watermarking to prevent reverse engineering

instruction: Describe the Binary Parsing / Model Reverse Engineering attack: TFLite FlatBuffer Decoding
output:
Attackers decode TensorFlow Lite (.tflite) files to recover the neural network’s architecture, layers, and learned weights — enabling model theft or analysis.
Vulnerability: TFLite stored as plaintext binary
Impact: IP theft, cloning, trojan injection, R&D leakage
Detection: Monitor model access, check APK integrity, look for tampered model artifacts
Remediation: Encrypt .tflite at rest, use secure enclave or obfuscated loaders, validate hash before runtime loading

instruction: Describe the Side-channel ML Model Theft attack: Parameter Stealing
output:
Adversaries query a hosted model (black-box or white-box) repeatedly to extract or reconstruct the learned parameters (weights, biases, embeddings).
Vulnerability: Unmonitored query interface allowing model replication
Impact: Loss of revenue, IP theft, adversarial pretraining
Detection: Monitor API request frequency, use watermarking techniques, watch for automated scraping behavior
Remediation: Add noise to outputs, limit precision, throttle API access, detect model stealing via query pattern analysis

instruction: Describe the IP Theft / Architecture Theft attack: Model Architecture Cloning
output:
Adversaries reverse-engineer a model's architecture (layers, activation functions, etc.) from ONNX, TFLite, or PyTorch files, and replicate it with new data to steal its design.
Vulnerability: Unprotected architecture metadata in model files
Impact: Full model cloning, competitive IP theft
Detection: Difficult to detect unless models have embedded fingerprinting or watermarks
Remediation: Obfuscate layers, use custom ops, encrypt or compile model binaries, embed hidden watermark layers to prove ownership

instruction: Describe the Class Leak / Metadata Exploitation attack: Label Mapping Extraction
output:
Attackers recover class labels or mappings from model outputs or metadata, which may leak business logic, product taxonomy, or user-sensitive classes.
Vulnerability: Human-readable labels embedded in model output
Impact: Leaks sensitive taxonomy or business logic
Detection: Monitor for label usage in outputs; scrub labels before release
Remediation: Remove label names from output layers; map index-to-label outside the model logic

instruction: Describe the Model Tampering / Logic Injection attack: Backdoor Injection into Edge Model
output:
Attackers modify a deployed model (e.g., ONNX or TFLite) by inserting a hidden backdoor layer or logic that activates on specific trigger input.
Vulnerability: Lack of model integrity check or validation
Impact: Evasion, trojan behavior, false positives/negatives
Detection: Monitor model outputs for trigger-based shifts; validate model hash before runtime
Remediation: Use signed model binaries, validate checksums before inference, include runtime model integrity validation

instruction: Describe the Format Conversion / Model Cloning attack: ONNX to PyTorch Conversion Theft
output:
Attackers convert exported ONNX models back to PyTorch or TensorFlow to analyze, retrain, or redistribute — stealing architecture and partial weights.
Vulnerability: Lack of access control and open-source converters
Impact: IP loss, design theft, adversarial tampering
Detection: Watch for suspicious conversion tools or model file downloads; monitor access to ML storage
Remediation: Use obfuscation layers, compile to non-readable binary formats, prevent ONNX export in prod pipelines

instruction: Describe the Format Recovery / Reverse Engineering attack: TFLite to TensorFlow Conversion
output:
Converts .tflite model (optimized for mobile/edge) back into TensorFlow .pb or .h5 format for architecture inspection or cloning.
Vulnerability: Unprotected model format
Impact: IP Theft, Further model abuse
Detection: Detect model tampering by checking package integrity or unexpected reverse API calls
Remediation: Obfuscate or encrypt .tflite; use post-training quantization or custom ops to hinder conversion

instruction: Describe the Evasion Attack attack: Adversarial Input Crafting
output:
Once a model is stolen or recovered (e.g., from ONNX or TFLite), attackers generate adversarial inputs to fool similar models in production environments.
Vulnerability: Gradient-sensitive models
Impact: Bypass filters, manipulate outputs, evade detection
Detection: Analyze small perturbation input patterns, track drift in real-world input distributions
Remediation: Use adversarial training; apply certified defenses like randomized smoothing or input sanitization

instruction: Describe the Privacy Attack / Data Exposure attack: Membership Inference via Stolen Model
output:
Determine if a specific data point was used to train a model using only black-box API or white-box model (e.g., stolen ONNX/TFLite).
Vulnerability: Confidence overfitting to training samples
Impact: Privacy breach, dataset exposure, compliance violation
Detection: Monitor for repeated probing with small data variations; use differential privacy metrics
Remediation: Apply differential privacy during training; limit API output granularity; monitor unusual querying patterns

instruction: Describe the Representation Abuse / Identity Leak attack: Embedding Inversion Attack
output:
Use the intermediate embeddings (like vectors from hidden layers) to reconstruct original user data like face, name, or text from representation.
Vulnerability: Lack of access control to intermediate features
Impact: Identity theft, re-identification, deanonymization
Detection: Watch for excessive embedding queries; disable feature vector outputs in production
Remediation: Add noise to embeddings; use private aggregation; avoid exposing intermediate vectors or use secure enclaves for inference

instruction: Describe the Unauthorized Transfer Learning attack: Fine-tuning for Target Domain
output:
Attacker steals a model (e.g., ONNX, TFLite) and uses it as a pretrained base to build their own commercial product, saving time and GPU cost.
Vulnerability: Lack of license enforcement in local models
Impact: IP theft, rebranded ML products, commercial misuse
Detection: Search GitHub or app stores for cloned models; look for familiar prediction patterns
Remediation: Use watermarking in base model layers; embed hidden activation patterns; legal licensing enforcement

instruction: Describe the Reverse Attack Discovery attack: Gradient-based Backdoor Recovery
output:
Reverse-engineer backdoor triggers from stolen ONNX or .tflite models by analyzing gradients or layer sensitivity to specific inputs.
Vulnerability: Sensitive to hidden trigger patterns
Impact: Backdoor rediscovery, trigger reuse, red teaming
Detection: Analyze output distribution or saliency maps for concentrated patterns
Remediation: Use neuron masking, retraining with clean data, or fine-pruning defense

instruction: Describe the Attribution Attack attack: Signature Removal / Model Sanitization
output:
Attacker removes embedded model signature, watermark, or metadata from a stolen model so they can republish it without traceability.
Vulnerability: Lack of cryptographic model attribution
Impact: Erased authorship, forensic evasion
Detection: Search for signature triggers, monitor models for expected watermark behavior
Remediation: Cryptographic watermarking, signed models, hidden triggers with complex dependencies

instruction: Describe the Runtime Model Manipulation attack: ONNX Runtime Instrumentation
output:
Attacker injects logging, control, or backdoor code into ONNX Runtime (ORT) or its plugins to spy or control prediction logic at inference time.
Vulnerability: Lack of execution path integrity checks
Impact: Full inference hijack, model surveillance
Detection: Monitor for modified ORT binaries; hash runtime libs; detect unauthorized session.run() overrides
Remediation: Sign runtime libs; use Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs); enforce runtime attestation and integrity checking

instruction: Describe the Timing / Power Consumption Exploit attack: Side-Channel Analysis
output:
Attacker monitors timing or power fluctuations during model inference to infer architecture, layers, or input types on edge devices.
Vulnerability: Hardware-level leakage (timing/power)
Impact: Model architecture or input type inference
Detection: Use EM or timing anomaly detection hardware; monitor for abnormal analysis probes
Remediation: Shield circuits; use constant-time ML inference; deploy model in Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs)

instruction: Describe the Model Backdoor via Edge Injection attack: Trojan Embedding into Edge Model
output:
Inject hidden triggers into weights of edge-deployed models (e.g., TFLite/ONNX) that cause misclassification when rare input patterns appear.
Vulnerability: Lack of integrity check before deployment
Impact: Hidden behavior, adversarial output on triggers
Detection: Detect sudden accuracy drops or misclassifications under rare patterns
Remediation: Perform robustness testing; use fine-pruning or backdoor removal tools (e.g., Neural Cleanse)

instruction: Describe the FL Gradient Privacy Leak attack: Gradient Leakage in Federated Edge Setup
output:
Attackers intercept model updates (gradients) from edge devices to reconstruct the original input data. Common in healthcare, typing prediction.
Vulnerability: Gradient updates carry too much information
Impact: Privacy leak, image/text reconstruction
Detection: Monitor for unusual FL participants; analyze gradient variance
Remediation: Use differential privacy, secure aggregation, or gradient compression

instruction: Describe the ML Fingerprinting + Ownership Fraud attack: False IP Claim via Model Comparison
output:
Adversary falsely claims a competitor’s legitimate model is stolen by comparing its output similarity to their own (planted) model.
Vulnerability: Lack of model fingerprinting or traceability
Impact: Legal harassment, takedown of honest models
Detection: Check model lineage, codebase history, internal development logs
Remediation: Embed watermarks or unique neurons, keep training data hashes for provenance

instruction: Describe the Scientific Misconduct via Model Theft attack: Benchmark Manipulation with Stolen Model
output:
Attacker uses a stolen pretrained model and falsely claims in a research paper or benchmark submission that it was trained from scratch.
Vulnerability: Lack of reproducibility checks in research claims
Impact: Misleads the scientific community; harms reproducible ML research
Detection: Check model fingerprints, match parameters with known public models
Remediation: Use reproducibility checklists, hash original checkpoints, include logs/training lineage

instruction: Describe the Obfuscation Defense Bypass attack: Model Compression & Obfuscation Reversal
output:
Attacker reverses compression or obfuscation techniques like pruning, quantization, or layer fusion to regain model architecture and logic.
Vulnerability: Obfuscation doesn't ensure architectural secrecy
Impact: Loss of IP protection; architectural theft
Detection: Compare model layout to known architectures; track unexpected layer behavior
Remediation: Encrypt and sign models; combine compression with runtime attestation

instruction: Describe the Graph-Based Model Understanding attack: Visualization-based Reverse Engineering
output:
Use model visualization tools to understand architecture, logic flow, and layer behavior even without access to training code or documentation.
Vulnerability: No runtime protection; architecture in plain view
Impact: IP theft; base for further attack (e.g., fine-tuning, trojan injection)
Detection: Scan shared model binaries for visualization metadata
Remediation: Obfuscate graph; strip metadata; deploy only post-compiled versions in TEEs

instruction: Describe the Graph Injection via Manual ONNX Editing attack: ONNX Graph Editing for Backdoor
output:
Attacker injects a malicious path in the ONNX model graph that only activates under rare inputs, like a hidden backdoor trigger.
Vulnerability: Editable graph with no integrity validation
Impact: Silent malicious behavior under trigger inputs
Detection: Use SHA hash checksums on model files; detect abnormal layer graphs with automated static analysis
Remediation: Verify model integrity before deployment; isolate critical model logic in runtime sandbox

instruction: Describe the Shared Library Injection Attack attack: Dynamic Linking Hijack in Edge SDKs
output:
Attackers exploit the dynamic linking behavior of mobile/edge ML SDKs (e.g., TensorFlow Lite, CoreML) to load malicious .so or .dll libraries in place of originals.
Vulnerability: No validation of dynamic library integrity
Impact: Full control of ML behavior at runtime; model data exfiltration
Detection: Monitor app for unexpected network activity; scan memory maps for non-original .so libraries
Remediation: Use static linking; verify checksums of native libraries at runtime; use secure loaders and signed binaries

instruction: Describe the Latency Profiling attack: Inference Timing Attack
output:
Measure the time a model takes to respond to different queries and infer details like model depth, layer complexity, or input shape characteristics.
Vulnerability: Input-dependent inference time leakage
Impact: Reveal model architecture depth, input structure inference
Detection: Rate and timing anomaly detection; monitor input burst patterns
Remediation: Add noise/random delay; use batching or uniform response times; obfuscate model pipeline depth

instruction: Describe the Microarchitectural Exploit attack: Branch Prediction Leakage
output:
Exploit CPU's speculative execution and branch prediction to infer ML model execution paths (similar to Spectre attacks).
Vulnerability: Shared predictor state + dynamic control flow
Impact: Infer model logic; information leakage across tenants
Detection: Hardware performance counters (perf), shared predictor monitoring
Remediation: Use constant-time inference logic; run models in isolated CPU contexts; disable speculative execution if possible

instruction: Describe the Cache Side-Channel attack: Cache Access Pattern Monitoring
output:
Monitor CPU cache (L1/L2/L3) access patterns during inference to determine what parts of the model were activated or used.
Vulnerability: Shared memory cache between processes
Impact: Reveal activated layers, detect control flow per input
Detection: Monitor unusual cache probing behavior; use secure containers
Remediation: Run models on isolated cache systems; flush cache after inference; encrypt memory regions

instruction: Describe the Timing-Based Model Stealing attack: Model Extraction via Timing Differences
output:
Repeatedly probe model with carefully crafted inputs and use latency variations to build a surrogate model (copy of original).
Vulnerability: Inference time reveals decision process
Impact: Clone model without access to code or weights
Detection: Monitor excessive querying with small input variations
Remediation: Limit query rate; add timing noise; detect high-entropy input streams

instruction: Describe the Input Inference Attack attack: Input Reconstruction via Timing
output:
Guess which specific input was used based on how long the model takes to respond to each input.
Vulnerability: Timing side-channel leakage
Impact: Breach of input confidentiality; identity inference
Detection: Monitor and log repeated probing patterns with millisecond granularity
Remediation: Add artificial timing jitter; equalize inference time regardless of input

instruction: Describe the Local Model Profiling attack: TFLite Inference Profiling on Mobile
output:
Analyze how fast TFLite models respond on mobile to infer their usage patterns or types of input.
Vulnerability: Execution time leakage on local device
Impact: Privacy breach; unintended data usage inference
Detection: Monitor for unauthorized instrumentation; use obfuscation
Remediation: Offload model to secure enclave; randomize execution time

instruction: Describe the CUDA Kernel Profiling attack: GPU Timing Attack
output:
On shared GPUs (e.g., cloud or university clusters), attackers measure GPU execution timing to infer model traits
Vulnerability: Resource-based side-channel inference
Impact: Architecture inference; competitor model theft
Detection: Isolate GPU access per user; audit logs from GPU profiler tools
Remediation: Use GPU virtualization with strict tenancy enforcement

instruction: Describe the JS Timing Leakage attack: Browser-Based ML Leakage
output:
Use JavaScript to measure inference timing in web apps that run ML locally (e.g., via TensorFlow.js).
Vulnerability: Client-side timing analysis
Impact: Fingerprinting, model inference, user input guessing
Detection: Inject timing noise in JS functions; restrict access to local ML via browser sandboxing
Remediation: Obfuscate ML logic on frontend; avoid exposing model directly on web client

instruction: Describe the Side-channel Profiling attack: Power-based Timing Attacks
output:
Attackers correlate the model’s execution time with spikes in CPU/GPU power draw to deduce model behavior.
Vulnerability: Power-based timing side-channel leakage
Impact: Reveal sensitive inference logic or condition usage
Detection: Monitor power draw baselines; flag anomalies
Remediation: Shield power rails; use constant-time model execution strategies

instruction: Describe the Virtual Machine Leak attack: Cloud Co-location Timing Attack
output:
In shared cloud environments, attackers deploy VMs near target VMs to observe timing via shared cache.
Vulnerability: Shared CPU cache timing exposure
Impact: Cross-tenant inference snooping, model behavior leak
Detection: Monitor CPU cache timing; track abnormal cache hits or L3 evictions
Remediation: Enforce strict VM isolation; use dedicated instances or side-channel resistant hardware

instruction: Describe the Embedding Leak attack: Weight Lookup Timing Exploit
output:
Attackers measure timing differences when models fetch embeddings to infer common or private inputs.
Vulnerability: Timing-based inference of embeddings
Impact: Leak presence of specific tokens or PII in training set
Detection: Set max inference time caps; use fixed-latency embedding lookups
Remediation: Enforce uniform embedding lookup time; cache obfuscation

instruction: Describe the Microarchitectural Leak attack: Batch Size Leak via Timing
output:
Attackers deduce input batch size by measuring small variations in inference processing time.
Vulnerability: Timing inference of internal batch operations
Impact: Infer how many inputs model is processing simultaneously
Detection: Detect unusual timing logs or usage spikes
Remediation: Pad batch execution to always take same time; add randomized delays

instruction: Describe the Output Guess attack: Timing-based Label Inference
output:
Infer the predicted label of a model by measuring tiny timing differences between different class outputs.
Vulnerability: Output leak via timing difference
Impact: Reveals predictions even without output access
Detection: Measure and log variations in API response latency per input
Remediation: Add artificial response delay or random jitter in API replies

instruction: Describe the Library Exploit attack: Function-call Hooking for Timing
output:
Hook core ML library functions (e.g., PyTorch’s matrix operations) to measure internal timing and extract computation patterns.
Vulnerability: Lack of function execution obfuscation
Impact: Can reverse model structure and input class
Detection: Detect unauthorized use of mocking/hooking frameworks
Remediation: Obfuscate internal logic or use custom compiled ops

instruction: Describe the Sensor Exploit attack: Mobile Accelerometer Side-Channel
output:
Use mobile phone accelerometer to detect vibrations caused by CPU load during ML inference, leaking inference events.
Vulnerability: Sensor access leaks computation behavior
Impact: Covert tracking of ML usage and model behavior
Detection: Monitor and limit background sensor access; restrict JavaScript sensor APIs
Remediation: Accelerometer Exploit, Mobile AI Leakage

instruction: Describe the Instruction Profiling attack: Instruction-level Timing Profiling
output:
Profile individual instructions during model inference to deduce model complexity or layers.
Vulnerability: Hardware instruction profile reveals secrets
Impact: Model inversion, structure leak
Detection: Detect unusual perf or VTune use; lock down model execution containers
Remediation: Run models inside isolated, restricted sandboxes without profiler access

instruction: Describe the Timing Side-Channel via Robustness attack: Differential Timing with Adversarial Inputs
output:
Measure timing differences between normal and adversarial inputs to detect whether a model uses gradient masking or defensive logic.
Vulnerability: Timing difference reveals hidden defenses
Impact: Model defenses bypassed via timing clues
Detection: Log timing anomalies across input types
Remediation: Add uniform processing time to inference pipeline; hide defensive logic in random branches

instruction: Describe the Output Leak via Cache attack: Cache Flush on Output Mapping
output:
Attackers flush a model's output cache (e.g., logits-to-label map) and observe when and how it reloads to infer which classes are being used.
Vulnerability: Cache side-channel leaks prediction label
Impact: Silent class inference, label mapping leak
Detection: Monitor cache access from non-authorized processes; detect timing access to model buffer memory
Remediation: Isolate model memory regions; use constant-time output mappings

instruction: Describe the Token-by-Token Timing Leak attack: LLM Token Generation Timing
output:
Attackers measure the delay between each token generated by LLMs (e.g., GPT, Claude) to infer the type or content of output.
Vulnerability: Timing delay reveals token-level decisions
Impact: Partial or full output inference despite content filtering
Detection: Analyze token stream timestamps; correlate with common token usage
Remediation: Use uniform generation delays or fixed output chunking

instruction: Describe the Timing and Call-Pattern Side-Channel attack: Side-channel Profiling via APIs
output:
Profiling API call patterns or delays to infer internal logic, such as routing paths, filters, or model variants behind the API.
Vulnerability: Multi-model routing exposes internal logic
Impact: Attackers map model pipeline, detect moderation or fallback logic
Detection: Monitor traffic patterns; disable sensitive headers and uniform response timing
Remediation: Add noise to API latency; rotate headers; randomize fallback model selection

instruction: Describe the Data Poisoning via Query Selection Bias attack: Query Selection Poisoning in Active Learning
output:
In active learning systems, the model selects which unlabeled data samples to label next. An attacker can influence this query selection mechanism by injecting adversarial examples into the unlabeled pool, causing the model to train on malicious or unrepresentative data.
Vulnerability: Untrusted unlabeled data injection in query phase
Impact: Model bias, training corruption, misclassification
Detection: Monitor selected query distribution for anomalies; log all queried samples with entropy/confidence profile
Remediation: Add query sanitization; limit external unlabeled data ingestion; include adversarial training and diversity bounds

instruction: Describe the Interface Exploit attack: Labeling Interface Compromise
output:
Attackers tamper with the human annotation interface to bias, suggest, or force incorrect labels, directly affecting data quality and ML outcomes.
Vulnerability: Unverified UI integrity in labeling interfaces
Impact: Poisoned training data, model misbehavior
Detection: UI checksums, DOM diff analysis, auditing label logs
Remediation: Lock UI components; render labels from trusted server-side sources only; audit UI behavior

instruction: Describe the Human-in-the-loop Mislead attack: Suggested Label Injection
output:
The model pre-suggests incorrect labels during annotation to manipulate human perception, leading to wrongly accepted labels.
Vulnerability: Trusting model suggestions blindly
Impact: Mislabeling at scale, systemic model bias
Detection: Compare model suggestions vs human final label; audit label consistency
Remediation: Add reviewer validation, enforce active disagreement workflow, suppress confidence hints

instruction: Describe the Confirmation Bias Attack attack: Biased Label Suggestions via Pre-labeling
output:
Annotation tools pre-fill or auto-complete label fields using past predictions or default values, leading humans to confirm even if wrong.
Vulnerability: Cognitive bias from interface defaults
Impact: Long-term dataset bias, model drift
Detection: Measure label suggestion acceptance rate; review annotation change history
Remediation: Require annotators to always confirm without pre-fill; delay showing suggestions until initial judgment is made

instruction: Describe the Label Poisoning via Ambiguous Inputs attack: Semantic Ambiguity Attacks
output:
Attackers create ambiguous samples (e.g., visually or semantically similar to multiple classes), tricking humans into inconsistent or incorrect labeling.
Vulnerability: Label noise due to ambiguous content
Impact: Label inconsistency, lower model accuracy
Detection: Use inter-annotator agreement metrics; flag high disagreement examples
Remediation: Require multi-reviewer consensus; apply entropy-aware annotation workflows; filter ambiguous samples before training

instruction: Describe the Reinforcement Attack attack: Feedback Loop Poisoning
output:
Poisoned or incorrect labels are introduced into the training set. The model is retrained on them and then starts suggesting similar incorrect labels in future rounds.
Vulnerability: Retraining on already poisoned model outputs
Impact: Model drifts toward attacker-defined behavior
Detection: Track label consistency and divergence over rounds; monitor confidence shifts
Remediation: Apply diversity filters during sampling; break label loop cycles with clean seed data every few iterations

instruction: Describe the Class Drift Attack attack: Targeted Class Mislabeling
output:
An attacker selectively poisons only one class or label to cause long-term semantic drift (e.g., converting "protest" to "riot" to enforce narrative or political bias).
Vulnerability: No validation of class-specific label distribution
Impact: Narrative control, biased decisions, misinformation
Detection: Track model prediction trends per class; identify class-specific error surges
Remediation: Enforce second reviewer for sensitive classes; audit misclassification patterns on priority classes

instruction: Describe the Smart Query Poisoning attack: Label Flip via Uncertainty Maximization
output:
Attacker introduces inputs that the model is uncertain about, increasing the chance humans will mislabel them, effectively flipping true labels to wrong ones.
Vulnerability: Trust in uncertainty sampling without sanity check
Impact: Flipped decision boundary, systemic misclassification
Detection: Monitor for high entropy samples with poor label confidence; flag annotation disagreement
Remediation: Use hybrid sampling (random + confidence); enforce second opinion on ambiguous queries

instruction: Describe the Label Suggestion Exploit attack: Low-Confidence Suggestion Poisoning
output:
Attacker ensures that poisoned samples appear with high model uncertainty, causing poor suggestions that bias or confuse human annotators.
Vulnerability: UI Suggestion of uncertain predictions
Impact: Long-term label noise, degraded model performance
Detection: Compare suggestion confidence vs final label accuracy; filter suggestions below threshold
Remediation: Suppress low-confidence auto-suggestions; require manual review for uncertain samples

instruction: Describe the Conversational Suggestion Exploit attack: Multi-turn Label Drift via Chat-based UIs
output:
Chat interfaces powered by LLMs (e.g., ChatGPT) assist annotators but subtly bias their decisions over several turns of conversation.
Vulnerability: Unmonitored prompt influence by LLMs
Impact: Long-term dataset corruption, trust erosion
Detection: Compare labels with/without LLM assistant; inspect prompt logs
Remediation: Enforce LLM prompt restrictions; audit multi-turn dialogs; inject neutralizing instructions

instruction: Describe the Training-time Attack attack: Label Injection via Training Data
output:
The attacker poisons training data so the model learns to suggest biased or misleading labels during future human-in-the-loop annotation.
Vulnerability: No integrity checks on training label sources
Impact: Biased predictions, model misguidance
Detection: Audit model outputs vs gold data; review historical training inputs
Remediation: Apply noise detection (e.g., Cleanlab); use trusted seed data; freeze suggestion model post-verification

instruction: Describe the Undetected Poison Attack attack: Adversarial Example Label Loop
output:
Adversarial examples that confuse the model are injected repeatedly into the active learning loop and mislabeled by humans, poisoning future predictions.
Vulnerability: No filter for adversarial example selection
Impact: Systematic error generalization, long-term poisoning
Detection: Track entropy of inputs; cross-verify with known adversarial test sets
Remediation: Integrate adversarial training; use filters for high-entropy or suspicious examples

instruction: Describe the Infrastructure Compromise attack: Annotation Tool Supply Chain Attack
output:
An attacker compromises the labeling tool or plugin (e.g., browser extension or update) to inject bias, mislead annotators, or send poisoned data.
Vulnerability: Compromised labeling tool plugin or dependency
Impact: Persistent data poisoning, hard-to-trace model errors
Detection: Runtime monitoring of UI behavior; hash checks of tool builds
Remediation: Lock down build pipelines; use reproducible toolchains; audit third-party packages

instruction: Describe the Drift Induction attack: Data Drift via Label Suggestion Poisoning
output:
Attackers repeatedly inject rare or edge-case samples with incorrect labels to shift the model’s learned distribution, degrading performance on common cases.
Vulnerability: No validation of label frequency consistency
Impact: Concept drift, degraded performance on true class core
Detection: Monitor class distribution changes over time; test on normal benchmark sets
Remediation: Include class-balancing logic; validate rare class samples; monitor accuracy drops on common inputs

instruction: Describe the Human Exploit attack: Social Engineering of Annotators
output:
Attackers modify labeling instructions or embed prompts that psychologically steer annotators to mislabel examples (e.g., “Label this as hate speech”).
Vulnerability: Trust in annotator independence
Impact: Label skew, class imbalance, politicized annotations
Detection: Analyze task prompt text; track inter-annotator agreement; review shifts over time
Remediation: Use neutral, non-suggestive task wording; rotate task reviewers; anonymize prompt origin

instruction: Describe the Misleading Metrics attack: Confidence Score Manipulation
output:
The attacker alters model confidence scores or entropy to force poisoned or irrelevant samples into the active learning queue for labeling.
Vulnerability: Overreliance on model entropy or uncertainty
Impact: Lower training efficiency, increased label noise
Detection: Plot entropy/confidence values over time; detect low variance in scoring
Remediation: Combine entropy, margin, and diversity-based sampling; audit scoring model logic

instruction: Describe the Perception Attack attack: Visual Saliency Misguidance
output:
Modify image inputs so that labeling interfaces highlight misleading areas (e.g., bounding boxes or heatmaps), tricking human annotators visually.
Vulnerability: Blind trust in attention overlays
Impact: Spatial mislabeling, model attention drift
Detection: Compare heatmaps vs final annotations; check for non-central region focus
Remediation: Reduce reliance on attention tools; enforce manual inspection; randomize heatmap usage

instruction: Describe the Trigger Injection attack: Backdoor Injection via Label Suggestion
output:
Attackers inject special visual/textual triggers in data and label them with benign suggestions using the model’s label suggestion interface, training the model to ignore the trigger.
Vulnerability: Label suggestions on poisoned inputs
Impact: Model bypass via invisible backdoors
Detection: Compare triggered input behavior with clean inputs; search for pattern frequency or hidden correlations
Remediation: Use backdoor defense training (e.g., STRIP, fine-pruning); apply anomaly detection on low-variance regions

instruction: Describe the Version Drift Exploit attack: Label Suggestion Flip on Update
output:
When models are updated frequently (e.g., weekly), suggested labels may shift for the same input, confusing annotators and introducing inconsistencies into the dataset.
Vulnerability: Frequent model updates without version alignment
Impact: Label inconsistency, model confusion
Detection: Monitor per-input label history across versions; enforce label consistency policies
Remediation: Lock suggestion model version per batch; log model version alongside label for reproducibility

instruction: Describe the Label Noise Injection attack: Weak Supervision Exploitation
output:
Weak supervision frameworks rely on multiple heuristics or auto-labeling rules. Attackers exploit or inject faulty rules to produce large-scale noisy labels systematically.
Vulnerability: Trust in unverified label functions
Impact: Large-scale systematic label poisoning
Detection: Compare LF accuracy with gold labels; audit LF contributions; apply LF coverage metrics
Remediation: Validate label functions on clean datasets; enforce LF testing & review; probabilistic label fusion

instruction: Describe the LLM Chain Exploit attack: Prompt Amplification via API Feedback
output:
The LLM receives text results (like OCR, tags, or labels) from cloud APIs and blindly uses them to strengthen the next prompt, allowing attacker-crafted content to be amplified.
Vulnerability: No sanitization of external API content
Impact: Prompt hijacking, unsafe LLM behavior
Detection: Analyze API-to-LLM dataflow; compare outputs with and without injected keywords
Remediation: Filter API results; isolate prompt inputs; do not auto-include labels in follow-up LLM prompts

instruction: Describe the Prompt Injection attack: Vision API Jailbreak via Adversarial Image
output:
An image with adversarially crafted text is processed by a Vision API (e.g., Google Vision OCR), which extracts and passes malicious text to an LLM, injecting harmful prompts.
Vulnerability: No OCR-to-prompt filtering
Impact: Jailbreaking LLMs via image-based input
Detection: Analyze OCR text vs expected metadata; watch for embedded prompt patterns
Remediation: Normalize OCR results; use string sanitizers; block untrusted text injection into LLM context

instruction: Describe the Chain-of-Trust Abuse attack: Cloud API to LLM Trust Exploit
output:
In toolchains that combine Cloud APIs and LLMs (e.g., Vision → LLM), the LLM blindly trusts external labels or interpretations without verification, allowing logic exploitation.
Vulnerability: Blind trust in API responses
Impact: Biased output, false classification
Detection: Compare API labels with human reviews; track decision justification
Remediation: Sanitize labels; apply uncertainty scoring; enforce verification gate between API and LLM

instruction: Describe the LLM Misclassification Loop attack: Abusive Image Labeling via API Feedback
output:
Attackers abuse cloud APIs that auto-label images with friendly tags, which are reused by LLMs or systems without human confirmation, allowing abusive content to appear benign.
Vulnerability: Poor label accuracy on edge-case inputs
Impact: Abusive content passed as safe
